> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The Transaction Recycler provides the ability to retry failed financial transactions again at regular intervals. This is a generic retry mechanism which can be consumed by any Temenos Transact application. The Transaction Recycler is available for Arrangement Architecture (AA) and Interest and Charged (IC) modules (R13 release and above). Read Transaction Cycler section under Settlement Property Class for more information related to Arrangement Architecture.

The Transaction Recycler service handles the retry of failed transactions. This service will run as a COB job at a specific stage during both End of Day (EOD) and online phases. This job will retry the transactions on scheduled dates until the transaction is settled or number of retry attempts allowed have been exhausted or retry end date is reached.

During each retry, the Transaction Recycler will take the amount available in the settlement account for settling the transaction amount in full or partial, based on the Transaction Recycler retry configuration. The RC can retry the settlement based on pre-defined priority order as defined by the bank. In case of an AA loan repayment, the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application allows the user to define sorting priority criteria based on custom values - the bill type or the aging status of bill.

The transactions handed over to Recycler (RC), if settled outside the RC framework are not excluded from further processing by RC and is marked with a specific status.

The following chart shows the transaction recycler process:

The Transaction Recycler acts as a framework and the processing required for retrying an AA payment or IC charges is built as a plug-in. In the above flow chart, the core plug-ins are generally represented as the payment processor, and the RC processes further, when there is an AA payment or an IC payment pending. The Transaction Recycler recognises that two different types of payments should be processed and the respective payment processor invoked is parameterised. This design enables the addition of new activity types (including any client-specific local activities) to be retried while using the same Transaction Recycler framework to orchestrate the recycling.


##### Product Configuration

The following chart shows the Transaction Recycler module components:

| Core Routine Fields | Description | Routine Name |
|---|---|---|
| Pre processor | Used to define whether a message specific core routine needs to be called to pre-process a message. | RC.PREP.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PREP.IC.CHARGE |
| Prioritise | Used to define the message-specific core routine called by the Transaction Recycler to perform transaction grouping and sorting. | RC.PRTY.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PRTY.IC.CHARGE |
| Processor | Used to define the message-specific core routine called by the Transaction Recycler to process the Transaction Recycler transaction, or transactions if they are grouped. | RC.PROC.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PROCE.IC.CHARGE |
| Post process | Defines the message-specific API routine called by the Transaction Recycler to perform processing after the transaction has been completed. | RC.POST.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.POST.IC.CHARGE |

The RC.PRIORITY application is a highest level prioritisation parameter that allows to setup priority of transactions at the company level by EB.SYSTEM.ID or AA.PRODUCT.GROUP . This application is used in conjunction with RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY and RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY to create the rules regarding which type of transaction takes priority when there is more than one outstanding transaction against a settlement account. It ranks by EB.SYSTEM.ID , by AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or by a custom RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record and the ID to this application can be either a master or a lead company.

In the RC.PRIORITY application, the order of priorities are defined in the descending order (for example, the first definition has the highest priority and so on).

- In the above screenshot, the system is set up to consider the transactions in the following order, if multiple retry requests are posted against the same account:First: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the PRIORITY+ONE record (direct debits sent by TPH with transaction code 125).

- Second: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the MORTAGES record (MORTGAGE AA Product and then MORTGAGE.CASHBACK AA Product).

- Third: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the PRIORITY +TPH record (direct debits sent by TPH with transaction code 213).

- Fourth: Request posted by the PAYMENT.ORDER application, irrespective of the request type.

When using as a priority, either a System ID (an EB.SYSTEM.ID record), the system does not require a correspondent RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record. If the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record is not defined, it will process all retry transaction requests posted by the application in a default order, considering the oldest one received by the recycler first.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system allows only one option for each priority to be entered. This can either be an EB.SYSTEM.ID, an AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or a Product Priority (custom RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY ID ).

Def Prev Settle is a filtering rule that means if, out of a list of ‘n’ pending transactions, one of transactions could not be settled (during retry), then all subsequent pending transactions in that list will be abandoned. It could be set to either Yes or No or left blank. If selected, it is applicable for EB.SYSTEM.ID , AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or Product Priority. This field is mutually exclusive with Prev Settle field.

The Prev Settle field can be set as Yes or No. If set to Yes, during retry of ‘n’ transactions, all transactions must be settled. Even if one of the transactions fail for some reason, then none of the remaining transactions will be considered for settlement.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application is used in conjunction with RC.PRIORITY and RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY to create the rules regarding the type of transaction that takes priority when there is more than one outstanding transaction against a settlement account. The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY is used to set the ranks at transaction level for the same type of retry request. It is used to set priority by value date, transaction amount or by a custom setting, for example by bills overdue status sent to Recycler by Arrangement Architecture (AA).

For example, if there are several transactions for the same product type against the settlement account, then the transactions have to be prioritised.

- The oldest transactions are processed first.
- If there are more than one transaction due for the same date and type, then prioritise by the largest amount first.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application allows the user to define sorting priority criteria based on custom values. For example, based on the bills’ status issued by AA in case of loans repayments. To perform this, set:

- Due Type - Sort By Priority Attribute
- Due Rule - Custom

The Priority Rank Type field in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY accepts the following three options:

- Aging Status - Enables prioritisation based on the aging status of bills generated for each arrangement.
- Bill Type - Enables prioritisation of bill ( RC.DETAIL ) records based on the bill type of the arrangements.
- Blank – The value is used if the prioritization is by Aging Status of the bills.

It is not possible to set the prioritization by both Aging Status /Blank and Bill Type in the same record.

The multi-valued Custom Priority Rank field must contain custom values in the order which they must be sorted. Based on the Custom Priority Rank the Custom Priority Rank field must contain valid EB.LOOKUP record values from AA.OVERDUE.STATUS or from AA.BILL.TYPE .

In the example below, the custom values represent the overdue bill’s status based on aging / bill type as they are sent by AA to Recycler, to process the retry requests.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is not possible to set the prioritization by both Aging Status / Blank and Bill Type in the same record.

The overdue status is shown in the RC.DETAIL record after the request is settled.

> **⚠️ Note:** The AA Payment Rules setup must be in sync with the setup done in the Recycler priority setup tables. For example, if the oldest bill setup is done in AA Payment Rules, the same setup must be done in the recycler.

For example, if the Payment Rules are setup to consider the oldest bill first for an AA Product, and for the same AA Product, the contract priority rule is setup to consider the largest amount first (different setup than in Payment Rules), the system works as follows:

- If two bills are issued for the same contract on the same date, the system settles the bills by date (oldest one first) ignoring the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for the same contract on different dates, the system settles the bills considering the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for different contracts on different dates, the system settles the bills considering the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for different contracts on the same date, the system settles the bills by date (oldest one first) ignoring the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.

The user can define product priorities based on contract custom criteria using the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application. If the user wants to define such priority, the Rank Based Priority field must be defined with the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY custom name. If this is set, the order defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY is applied to all products setup in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY . For example, it is possible to define custom priority criteria based on bills overdue status and based on product type. The bills overdue status should be setup first in the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application as a custom record (read the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY for more details).

In order to sort the retry request based on the setup in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY and the one in the product order defined in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY , Priority Execution field must be defined. The values in this field are ’Rank Then Product’ and ’Product Then Rank’.

If the value ’Rank Then Product’ is selected, if more than one retry request is posted against the same account, the system orders requests based on the rank (status) defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY first and then by the product as defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY . If the value ’Product Then Rank’ is selected, the system orders the requests by product first and then by their rank from the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application.

The following screenshot shows the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY is created with the value ’Rank Then Product’.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY custom record ‘MORTGAGELOANS’ has the setup as shown in the below screenshot.

The RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record is setup to order the requests according to the rank (status) first and then according to the product order (MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD and then MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y), if more than one request has the same rank (status).

In case the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record has a custom ID and if the Priority Execution field is defined with the value ’Rank Then Product’, the Aa Product Group field will become multivalued, allowing the definition of priorities based on products which are part of different AA PRODUCT GROUPS in the same record.

The input of Aa Product Group field is mandatory in case any Aa Product are defined. The Aa Product definition is not mandatory if the Aa Product Group is entered. If only the Aa Product Group is defined, the system considers all the retry requests posted by any product type within the product group and orders them by date (the oldest one is considered first). It is not possible to define a duplicate combination of Aa Product Group and Aa Product of the same type in the same record.

The online recycler checks for the following:

- New triggers on the accounts with active retry requests.
- Retry request for which the cut off time has passed.

The RC.PARAMETER application controls the retry trigger and the Create Retry Trigger field can have one of the following options:

- Any Credit – The system creates a retry trigger ( RC.RETRY.TRIGGER table application) for any credit posted on the account.
- Credit Balance – The system creates a retry trigger only if the new credit makes the account balance positive.

In the OVERRIDE record, ACCT.UNAUTH.OD, the Susp Appln field and Fwd Acct Mode should to be configured, as shown in the example below:

| Scenario 1 Schedule Initiation on Holiday parameter is configured | Scenario 2 Schedule Initiation on Holiday parameter is not configured |
|---|---|
| Transaction Recycler retries the transaction to settle the bill. System checks the value date when the settlement account received the funds. As it is backdated, RC settles the bill with value date on Saturday. Penalty interest accrued for Saturday and Sunday is reversed, and only one day of penalty interest is applied to the contract. Bill is settled & Contract status = Current, as of Saturday. | Transaction Recycler retries the transaction to settle the bill. System checks the value date when the settlement account received the funds. As it is backdated, RC settles the bill with the value date on Saturday. Age Overdue activity is reversed and not replayed. Total amount for which the customer is charged = Instalment amount + One day’s penalty. Due to the reversal of the ageing activities, the penalty interest is posted to UNC/remainder activity. |


##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as ‘Yes’, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Transaction Recycler.

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|
| settlementService.transactionRetry.currentRetry | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is moved to current status |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundRecovered | Event to be emitted for a transaction retry when the funds are recovered successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundReserved | Event to be emitted for a transaction retry when the funds are reserved successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.manuallyApproved | Event to be emitted when a transaction is manually approved |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCancelled | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is cancelled |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCompleted | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is completed |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCreated | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is created |


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PARAMETER`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY`

#### 📖 Introduction

The add-on services or subscriptions such as insurance, extended warranty, roadside assistance, maintenance, and servicing can be bundled into the Asset Finance thus enabling the bank to offer an end-to-end operational service under one roof for invoice, billing, and settlement. Besides, this feature enables the banks or financial institutions to provide a variety of options for the customer to manage the subscriptions in the financial arrangements.

The subscription fee is a flat fee for each subscription and it is determined based on the pricing grid conditions. The subscription fee can either be a one-off or a recurring payment at specified intervals, continuing until a certain period or the contract end date.

The Subscriptions lifecycle is depicted below:

A high-level workflow to add subscriptions in the finance arrangement is shown below:


##### Product Line Attributes

The Subscriptions product line supports the following line attributes:

- Currency – Supports currency-specific product conditions.
- No Arrangements - Arrangements cannot be created.


##### Product Configuration

The following section describes the product configuration required for Subscriptions products.


##### Property Classes

The Accounting property class is a mandatory property class for the Subscription product line. It defines the accounting rules for the subscription product and controls the link between the accounting events generated by the property actions and the accounting allocation rules to be applied to these events. In Allocation rules, the LEASE-CHARGE record is applicable for the accounting of subscriptions fees.

The Pricing Grid Property class is mandatory for the Subscription product. The subscription fee is calculated based on the configuration of the pricing grid product condition. The Pricing Grid product condition can be defined with the data elements such as Finance amount, Term, Asset class, Asset type, Risk rating and so on and the target component as Charge amount (flat). Read Configuring Fee Grid and Introduction to Data and Target Elements for more information on Pricing Grid property class and attributes.

The Tax Property Class can be optionally configured in subscription products for VAT on the subscription fees. It primarily controls the VAT applicable subscription product.

Read Configuring Taxation to know about the tax configuration.


##### Product Builder

Read Introduction to Product Builder User Guide for more information on product construction and configuration process.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters


###### Facility Property in Financial Product

The financial product’s Facility property is configured with the new Subscriptions Supported property type to define the allowed subscription group, subscription plan, and variation for the financial product in the Facility product condition of the financial product. If Property Type is not set as Subscriptions Supported, the fields mentioned above cannot be configured.


###### Pricing Grid Property in Subscription Product

The pricing grid property is configured with the Property Type set as Subscription Supported. The pricing grid property defines the pricing of the subscription product. Upon adding the subscription product in the financial arrangement, the system derives the fee amount based on the criteria. Upon raising the bill/invoice in the financial arrangement, the system uses the charge property that is attached in the Linked Property attribute of the pricing grid property record.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Linked Charge property is allowed only when Pricing Grid property’s Property Type is set as Subscriptions Supported.


###### Charge Property

The charge property is attached as a linked property in the Pricing Grid property. This charge property‘s Property Type is set as Subscription Supported.


##### Illustrating Model Products

The following model products are reference products for the user to use, amend, or refer when creating new Subscription products.

| Product Name | Product Attributes |
|---|---|
| Insurance | Payment Protection (AXA) Residual Guarantee (ALD Auto) Roadside Assistance (ALD Auto) |
| Maintenance | Service Plan (ALD Auto) Service Plan (D&G) |

### 2.2  Subscriptions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The subscriptions feature enables the banks or financial institutions to provide a variety of options for the customer to manage the subscriptions in the financial arrangements. The user can add, modify, and cancel the subscriptions to the financial arrangement. The subscription fee can be either be...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement Date*, *Alternate Id*, *Amount*, *Asset Reference*, *Bill Produced*, *Change Date Type*, *Change Period*, *Criterion Id* ... +23 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The subscriptions feature enables the banks or financial institutions to provide a variety of options for the customer to manage the subscriptions in the financial arrangements. The user can add, modify, and cancel the subscriptions to the financial arrangement. The subscription fee can be either be a one-off or a recurring payment at specified intervals, continuing until a certain period or the contract end date


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Subscription product must be configured with Accounting, Pricing Grid properties and optionally with Tax property. Also, variations are allowed in the Subscription products.

The Pricing Grid product condition is configured with the criteria ( Criterion Id ) as Finance amount and the target component ( Target Id ) as Fixed charges.

The payment rule must be configured in the financial product to settle the subscription invoices generated in the financial arrangement. The Property Class attribute in the Payment Rules property class helps to define the Charge property class. The system allocates payments in the sequence order of the properties followed by the property class. The Property Class can only be defined as the last item in the sequence.

The system raises an error when the user attempts to define the Charge property class at the beginning or in the middle of the sequence.

Subscription products can be configured in the Facility product condition of the financial product to pre-define the allowed subscription products and variations that can be added in the financial arrangement. The set of attributes used to define the allowed subscription products in the facility property at financial product level are:

- Subscription Group - The user can select the product group available in the Subscriptions product line.
- Subscription - The user can select the subscription product available in the product group selected in the Subscription Group attribute.
- Variatio n - The user can select the variations available for the subscription product selected in the Subscription attribute.


#### 📋 Tasks

The subscriptions product line allows the user to add, modify, and cancel the subscriptions to the financial arrangement through the Subscription Services property class. The subscription fee can be collected on a periodic or on a one-time basis.


##### Workflow

In Subscriptions, the user can perform the following activities:

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
| Business Banking Operations | Finance Lease . Click the New Arrangement icon corresponding to the Finance Lease (Healthcare) Product. |
| New Arrangement | Subscription Services section, enter the value in the following attributes as required. Subscription Variation Alternate Id User Amt Payment Mode Start Date Term Expiry Date Frequency Bill Produced Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. Accept the overrides, if any. |
| Manager Login | Find Unauthorised Asset Finance Arragements . |
| Find Arrangement | Enter the Arrangement ID in Arrangement search criteria and click the Find button. |
| Overview Screen | Click the Overview icon. |
| Pending Approvals | Pending Approval . Select Approve option from the drill-down list corresponding to New Arrangement activity. |
| Authorise Transaction | Click the Authorise a deal icon to approve the activity. |


#### 📊 Outputs

The subscriptions product line allows the user to add, modify, and cancel the subscriptions to the financial arrangement through the Subscription Services property class. The subscription fee can be collected on a periodic or on a one-time basis.

### 3.2  Additional Features

#### 📖 Introduction

This section details the additional features in asset finance.


##### Backdate Constraints

The ASSET.FINANCE product line supports the addition of the Constraint property class to the asset finance products to manage and restrict backdated transactions.

Constraint PC restricts backdated adjustment from being posted in arrangements beyond the allowed period or date which could be either a set period, last payment date, last financial year or a specific date.


##### Cashback and Bonuses

The Asset Finance product line supports adding of credit type charge properties to the asset finance products. This allows banks and financial institutions to offer bonuses and cashbacks (using Temenos Asset Finance solution) if any, as part of a reward program. The user can set bonus/cashback to payout either as a one-off, periodic, or based on eligibility.

- Cash deposit of USD 500 towards Asset Purchase.
- Bonus of USD 50 for managing repayments on time.


##### Rule 78

Banks or Financial Institutions use the Rule 78 method to calculate payments or instalments in the Asset Finance arrangements. Read Rule 78 under the Configuration section for more information on the configuration of Rule 78 for Asset Finance arrangements.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration required for the additional features in asset finance.


##### Backdate Constraints

Asset Finance products can be configured with a restriction of backdate transaction using the Constraint Property Class. Read Constraint for more information on how to configure backdate restrictions.

The Constraint Property Class highlighted below blocks any transaction or activity when backdated beyond six months.


##### Cashback and Bonuses

This section describes the configuration of cashback and bonuses in Asset Finance product line.

The user can configure the BONUS property by setting Type as Credit and Property Class as CHARGE in AA.PROPERTY .

The user configure the property CASHBACK by setting Type as Credit and Property Class as CHARGE in AA.PROPERTY .

The user can define the property condition for BONUS property as shown below.

The user can define the property condition for CASHBACK property as shown below.


##### Rule 78

This section explains the configuration of the Rule 78 method.

Payment Type

To configure the payment type,

1. Configure the routine-based payment type to calculate Rule 78.
2. Configure the AA.CALCULATE.RULE78.PRIN.AMOUNT and AA.CALCULATE.RULE78.INTEREST.AMOUNT routines in the Calc Routine attribute with Calculation Type set as ‘Other’ in the Payment Type records for Principal and Interest respectively.
3. Define the Rule 78 payment types in the Payment Type attribute of the Payment Schedule product condition. After the above steps are completed, payment type is configured for Rule 78.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains how the additional features function in asset finance.


##### Backdate Constraints

The backdated asset finance transactions and activities can be controlled using the Constraint Property Class.

Read the Configuration section to understand the configuration.

Consider April 18, 2023 as the current Transact Date.

When the new arrangement activity is backdated beyond six months (that is, before October 18, 2022), the system blocks the activity.

When the new arrangement activity is backdated within six months (that is, up to October 18, 2022), the system allows the activity.

#### 📖 Introduction

- Welcome letter post activation of agreement.
- Payment remainder on ‘x’ days before every due date.
- Chaser notice for missed payments.
- Settlement quotation for simulating payoff.
- Notice for bank initiated forced terminations.
- Rate change notice ‘x’ days before change date or post-rate change.
- Payment confirmation.
- Maturity Remainder ‘x’ days before the maturity date.
- Amendment Notice – SSI, extension, regular payments.

### 3.5  Asset Management


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *As part of the Asset Finance solution, the Fixed Asset Management (FIXAMT) module is enhanced and seamlessly integrated with the Asset Finance (AS) module to manage the assets for financing. It enables banks and financial institutions to efficiently manage and finance both new and used assets. The a...*
> 
> **Applications:** `ASSET.DETAILS`, `ASSET.MAINTENANCE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Advanced Payment Type*, *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Arrangement ID*, *Asset Class*, *Asset Id*, *Asset Reference*, *Asset Type* ... +25 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

As part of the Asset Finance solution, the Fixed Asset Management (FIXAMT) module is enhanced and seamlessly integrated with the Asset Finance (AS) module to manage the assets for financing. It enables banks and financial institutions to efficiently manage and finance both new and used assets. The asset is linked to the asset finance arrangement in the arrangement creation stage (Refer the Introduction to Creating Arrangement section for more information on creating arrangements).

The asset linked with the asset finance arrangement follows the finance lifecycle and different statuses based on the events occurring in the asset finance arrangement throughout the term (that is, Activation, Maturity and so on). After the asset finance arrangement is activated, the asset can be purchased automatically by issuing a Payout to the supplier or vendor when the asset is not purchased already at the time of activation. When the arrangement matures, the asset can be repossessed or disposed based on the maturity option opted.

The below flow diagram provides an overview of integration touch points such as contract creation, activation, maturity, and termination.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Assets are classified to enable banks to group their fixed assets based on the asset characteristic nature, purpose and legal or depreciation requirements. Assets can be classified based on the following structure.


##### Asset Class and Asset Type

For Asset Class and Asset Type configurations, refer the Working with Fixed Asset Classification section.


##### Asset Maintenance

The asset can be captured and maintained in the ASSET.MAINTENANCE application using activities such as Register, Purchase and so on. In the asset finance solution, the Register activity can be triggered in the ASSET.MAINTENANCE application to register the asset. The system triggers the other applicable asset maintenance activities such as Purchase, Finance and Dispose upon the appropriate events in the asset finance arrangement.

The Avail for Finance attribute can be chosen for the asset that is registered for financing, meaning, the assets with the Avail for Finance attribute enabled can only be linked in the asset finance arrangement.


##### Registering the Asset

The asset can be registered in the ASSET.MAINTENANCE application with data such as Description , Asset Class , Asset Type , Depreciation Method , Depreciation Frequency , Avail for Finance and Third party Beneficiary Reference (that is, supplier or vendor beneficiary). An asset reference is allocated for the registered asset.

After the register activity is successfully completed, the system maintains the asset details in ASSET.DETAILS for processing.


##### Account PC

In Account PC, the Pay to Supplier attribute is available to control the purchase activity automatically when the asset is not purchased when the arrangement is activated.

The Pay to Supplier attribute determines whether the purchase of the asset occurs automatically by paying the supplier when the asset is not already purchased at the time of arrangement activation.

- Yes - Indicates the Asset Purchase takes place automatically by issuing the payment to the supplier during the activation and the asset status moves to ‘Purchased’.
- No or Blank - Indicates that during the activation, the Asset Purchase does not occur automatically if the asset is not already purchased and the contract activation is blocked.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the activities supported for the integration with fixed asset and the procedure to record or perform the activities in the system.


##### Linking Asset and Arrangement

To link the asset with the arrangement,

1. Create the asset finance arrangement by triggering the ASSET.FINANCE-NEW-ARRANGEMENT activity.
2. Link the asset with the arrangement using the Asset Reference attribute in Account Condition.
3. Select an asset from the list of assets available for financing (that is, assets marked with Avail for Finance as Yes in ASSET.DETAILS ) with the status as Registered or Purchased. The asset cannot be changed in the arrangement after authorising the arrangement.
4. After creating the arrangement, the respective asset's record in ASSET.DETAILS is updated in the Contract Type (Finance or Operating) and Contract Ref (Arrangement Reference) fields. This indicates that the link between the asset and the arrangement is established.
5. If the user tries to link that asset in a new arrangement when the asset is already linked to an arrangement, the system blocks the new arrangement activity by raising the error, ‘Asset is already linked to arrangement’.
6. If the user tries to link that asset which is not available for finance (that is, assets marked with Avail for Finance as No in the ASSET.DETAILS ) the system blocks the new arrangement activity by raising the error, 'Asset is not available for Financing'.
7. If the user tries to link the asset when the subject asset is not either ‘Registered’ or ‘Purchased’, the system blocks the new arrangement activity by raising the error, ‘Asset is not available for Financing’.


##### Arrangement Cancellation

If the arrangement is cancelled using the ASSET.FINANCE-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT activity, the system removes the respective arrangement's link details ( Contract Type and Contract Ref ) from the respective asset's record in ASSET.DETAILS . This indicates that the asset is delinked from the arrangement.

The arrangement data ( Contract Type and Contract Ref ) is removed from the asset records after the activity is successfully cancelled.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the unauthorised arrangement activity is deleted or the arrangement is reversed, the arrangement details are delinked from the respective asset's record in ASSET.DETAILS .


##### Activating the Arrangement

The system uses the FASUSPENSE balance type in the arrangement to transfer the amount to or receive the amount from Fixed Asset Management (FIXAMT) based on the events at the arrangement.

When the arrangement is activated using the ASSET.FINANCE-ACTIVATE-ARRANGEMENT activity, the system triggers the Asset Maintenance's finance activity which updates the Status of the asset as ‘Financed’ and raises appropriate entries in the arrangement. For the Purchase the Asset Option, the system debits the asset value from the CURLEASEPRINCIPAL, contract balance and credits the FASUSPENSE balance type.

- If the arrangement's commitment amount is greater than the asset value, then the system credits the asset cost to the FASUSPENSE balance type and realises the excess amount as adjustment or profit in the Profit and Loss (PL)account.
- If the arrangement's commitment amount is lesser than the asset value, then the system credits the asset cost to the FASUSPENSE balance type and realises the difference amount as adjustment or loss in the Profit and Loss (PL) account.

Refer Maturity Options under Asset Finance for more information on Purchase the Asset option.

The following are scenarios for Finance Lease:

| Asset Value | Commitment Amount |
|---|---|
| USD 23,000 | USD 25,000 |

### 3.6  Billing or Invoicing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A financial institution creates an asset finance arrangement for a customer and defines the terms and conditions for financing the asset (for example, medical equipment). The customer agrees to repay a fixed amount on a specific frequency throughout the agreed term. The system generates and sends th...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`, `EB.LOOKUP`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Bill Produced*, *Bills Produced*, *Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A financial institution creates an asset finance arrangement for a customer and defines the terms and conditions for financing the asset (for example, medical equipment). The customer agrees to repay a fixed amount on a specific frequency throughout the agreed term. The system generates and sends the bill or invoice for every repayment to the customer, on or before the due date (depending on agreed terms) for collection. The bill comprises of components such as principal, interest, charges or subscription fees and so on, as per the conditions negotiated at the time of setting up the arrangement.

By default, the system creates the bills on the due date, however the user can configure the Bill Produced attribute in the Payment Schedule condition to allow the system to issue the bill in advance.

When the system creates a bill or invoice, the bill goes through the following lifecycle:

- The Bill Status is initially marked as Issued (if issued a few days in advance), and then changed to Due, when the due date is reached.
- After the customer repays the bill in full, the status is marked as Settled.
- If the customer does not repay the bill in full, the status moves to Past due based on the setup in Overdue conditions.

Read Schedule of Payments for more information on payment schedule.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration for generating an invoice or bill in the asset finance arrangements.


##### Configuring Payment Schedule

The system generates the scheduled bills based on the Payment Schedule property conditions. To configure the payment type and payment schedule,

1. Configure the CONSTANT, PRINCIPAL, and INTEREST.ONLY payment types with the required payment frequencies in the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application.
2. Configure the Payment Schedule condition to generate the scheduled payments for the asset finance arrangement.

Refer Payment Schedule for more information on the Payment Schedule property class.

The business banking officer configures the Payment Schedule condition for the asset finance arrangement in the product setup to generate bills for regular payments which comprise of principal and interest components in the monthly interval or frequency. The user can also negotiate this setup in the payment schedule tab while creating the arrangement.

The user can also configure the charges such as maintenance fees, inspection fees and admin fees in the Payment Schedule property condition to create bills regularly on a defined frequency.

The Business Banking Officer configures an admin fee of USD 100 to be billed every six months in the Payment Schedule condition.


##### Issuing Bill in Advance

By default, the system creates the bills on the due date, however the user can configure the Bill Produced attribute in the Payment Schedule condition to allow the system to issue the bill in advance. In the Bills Produced attribute, the user can define the number of day(s) prior to the actual payment date.

Refer Payment Schedule for more information on Payment Schedule property class.


##### Changing Payment Schedule

Refer the Configuration section under Amend Payment Frequency in Midlife Amendments for more information on changing the frequency of the payments.


##### Configuring Activity Charges

The business banking officer defines event-based one-off charges like Arrangement fees, Documentation fees and so on, for a product using the Activity Charges property condition.

The Business Banking Officer configures a purchase fee of USD 500 to be collected when the asset finance arrangement is created.

Refer Activity Charges for more information on the Activity Charges property condition.


##### Overdue Processing

The system performs the past due or delinquency processing for unpaid bills based on the configurations in the Overdue product condition. The setup can either be specified in number of days or number of bills, past due. The financial institutions can soft-configure the overdue classifications as per their business requirement in the EB.LOOKUP application.

The business banking officer configures the overdue condition for an asset finance product.

If the bill is unpaid for:

- More than 30 days, classify it as standard
- More than 90 days, classify it as sub-standard
- More than 180 days, classify as doubtful
- More than 360 days, classify it as loss

Refer Overdue for more information on Overdue property class.


##### Sending Advice

The business banking officer configures the system to send the advice or correspondence to the customer, when the bill is generated.

Refer Activity Messaging for more information on the configuration for pre-notice, advice or correspondence to be sent to the end-customer using the Activity Messaging property class.


#### 🔧 Working With

The system generates the bills for the regular payments based on the Payment Schedule condition.

The following examples illustrate the workflow for billing and invoicing:

The business banking officer creates an asset finance arrangement for USD 10,000, for one year with regular monthly payments.

The system generates bills for the regular payment amount of USD 851.42 on the respective due date as shown in the bills section of the arrangement overview screen.

The Itemised by Property tab provides the components (that is, Principal of USD 755.36, Interest of USD 96.06, Charge and so on) involved in the bill, as shown in the screenshot below.

The Itemised by Payment Type tab provides the details of the payment types (set as Constant-Monthly for the bill date, March 27, 2023) involved in the bill as shown in the screenshot below.

The Status Timeline tab provides the details of the bill statuses from the bill date to the current system date.

The system performs the ageing of bills past due date based on the Overdue condition.

The system updates the Status field as Standard in the overdue processing, for the bills with payment dates as March 2, 2023 and February 2, 2023, as they are not repaid by the customers.

The bill for the payment date February 2, 2023 is in overdue status (Standard), which includes principal as USD 817.45 and interest as USD 33.97, as shown in the screenshot below.

In the screenshot below, the bill for the payment date March 2, 2023, is in overdue status (Standard), with principal as USD 823.24 and interest as USD 28.18.

As part of the overdue process, the system maintains the overdue balances in the overdue balance types in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES application as shown in the screenshot below.

### 3.7  Charges and Commissions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The charges or commissions are termed as fee. Financial institutions can calculate these fee as a flat or percentage of the finance amount, residual, or receivables, and the charge rate varies based on the amount tier (level or band).*
> 
> **Applications:** `ASSET.FINANCE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Payment Period*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks


#### 📖 Introduction

The charges or commissions are termed as fee. Financial institutions can calculate these fee as a flat or percentage of the finance amount, residual, or receivables, and the charge rate varies based on the amount tier (level or band).

The asset finance arrangement consists of the following charges:

1. One-off charges like upfront fee, documentation fee, and so on.
2. Regular or periodical charges such as service or maintenance fee and usage-based fee.

Financial institutions can collect the charges based on the occurrence of a specific activity, such as creation of an arrangement, or failure to collect the asset on the termination of the asset finance arrangement.

The chargeable amount can be in a specific currency which can be different from the currency of the account based on the business expectations. The financial institution can apply discount on the calculated charge before applying the pre-defined cap and floor amount. So, based on the configurations, the financial institution can waive the charge fully or partially and the system allocates the waived amount to a separate profit and loss category.

The various types of charges a financial institution can apply on asset finance arrangements are explained in the below table.

| Charges | Description |
|---|---|
| Commitment fee or arrangement fee | Fee for the committed finance amount at the time of an arrangement’s inception. The financial institution charges this fee as a flat amount (that is, USD 500) or as a percentage of the finance amount (0.2 percentage of the finance amount) and collects the fee at the time of an arrangement’s creation. |
| Application fee or document fee | Fee for processing an asset finance application. The financial institution charges this fee as a flat amount and usually collects this fee along with the first repayment. |
| Service or maintenance fee | Fee for maintaining or improving the assets and managing the insurance for the asset. The financial institution collects this fee on a periodic basis. For example, annual maintenance fee for a car. |
| Admin fee | Fee for administration activities, such as amending the interest rate, term, or providing ad-hoc statements to the lessee or primary customer. |
| Delivery Fee | Fee to deliver the asset at the lessee's location and the financial institution usually collects this fee along with the first repayment. |
| Purchase fee | Fee when a lessee or primary customer opts to buy the asset at the end of the term and the financial institution usually collects this fee along with the last repayment. |
| Collection failure fee | Fee charged as a penalty when a customer fails to return the asset on the agreed return date (the date can be term end or maturity date). |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Charge property class captures the details of the document fees, upfront charges and so on. The asset finance arrangement consists of the following charges:

1. One-off charges like upfront fee, documentation fee, and so on.
2. Regular or periodical charges such as service or maintenance and usage-based fees.

These charges can either be flat or calculated based on the balance or transaction amount.


##### Configuring Payment Period

The users can configure the activity charges, to collect it along with the regular repayments. This feature also facilitates the collection of billed charges along with the first, next, and last repayments. The Payment Period attribute in the Activity Charges property class is used to configure the payment period. The options available for the payment period are:

- First payment
- Next payment
- Last payment

For example, When a user opts for the first payment, the billed charge amount is due along with the first repayment bill and respectively for each payment period selected.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Payment Period attribute is applicable only for ASSET.FINANCE product line.

Read Charges for more information on charge property class.


##### Pricing Grids

Asset Finance supports Rate Cards (Pricing Grids product line) for defining Charge definitions. Read Fee Grid for more information on Fee Grid.


#### 🔧 Working With

The users can configure the charges to be due on the first, next, or last payment. The charges are triggered on occurrence of a specific activity and it is due to the customer as per the configuration.

If a user has set the charge collection on the next payment, but the system levies the charge on creation of the contract, it is still due only on the next payment date, that is, it is not due immediately. It is scheduled to be collected on the first payment date as per the schedule configuration.

Alternatively, if a user configures the collection of charge on the first payment, but the first payment date lapses when the customer triggers an activity, the system raises an override and schedules the charge along with the next upcoming payment.


##### Collecting Fee for External Event

The Record Event activity class registers an external event manually in the system. In asset financing, the financial institution can collect a delivery fee when the asset is delivered to the lessee or customer. This is an external event and not connected to the system. The user can manually register the event in the system using ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT. Similarly, below activities are used for collecting charges for external events:

- Failed collection of the asset: At the end of the term, if the lessor is unable to collect the asset, the financial institution levies a charge for the failure of collection of assets. The activity can be registered in the system using ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.FAILED.COLLECTION-ARRANGEMENT activity. A failed collection fee is levied on the arrangement when the user triggers this activity manually.
- Payment return fee: Lease payments scheduled for collection from an external system might fail due to various reasons like account unavailability or insufficient funds. System triggers ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.DD.RETURN-ARRANGEMENT activity to register the payment failure. The user can configure a payment return fee on occurrence of this activity.

User creates an arrangement with the condition that the system collects the delivery fee when the ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered.

Delivering the asset to the lessee is an external event. The user triggers ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT in the system to register this external event. System prompts an alert message that a fee is levied for the activity.

System schedules the delivery fee to be collected along with the first payment.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for the Charges and Commissions feature.


> **Related Applications:** `ASSET.FINANCE`

### 3.8  Covenants and Conditions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The covenants and conditions is a promise that needs to be honoured by the counterparty or lessee to activate and continue the asset finance agreement. The customer must submit the covenant, which is validated on an agreed frequency. A condition is validated when activating the arrangement.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.CLASS.DEFINITION`, `AA.DEFINITION.MANAGER`, `EV.DES.<EVIDENCE.NAME>`, `EV.EVIDENCE`, `EV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT`, `EV.REQUIREMENT.CATEGORY`, `RESTRICT.ACTIVATION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Class Type*, *Consequence*, *Notice Days*, *Process Method*, *Publish Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The covenants and conditions is a promise that needs to be honoured by the counterparty or lessee to activate and continue the asset finance agreement. The customer must submit the covenant, which is validated on an agreed frequency. A condition is validated when activating the arrangement.

The covenants and conditions allow the bank or financial institution to have control over the asset. When an arrangement is activated, the financial institution defines certain mandatory covenants and conditions that the lessee needs to submit to activate the arrangement. If the lessee fails to submit these documents, they have to deal with the corresponding consequence of not meeting the required conditions.

In asset finance, the covenants and conditions play a major role in activating the arrangement and maintaining insurance certificates, inspection, and quarterly financial statement of the lessee or primary customer.

The lessee is non-compliant in the below scenarios:

- Conditions – Activation of an arrangement can be restricted if the lessee does not acknowledge the certificate of acceptance.
- Covenant – Quarterly financial statement is not submitted, and the lessee does not meet the debt service ratio. For example, the bank criteria expects the lessee to initially maintain a debt service ratio of less than 0.5%.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Evidence property class is configured to check the covenants and conditions in the life cycle of the asset finance arrangement. Evidence is validated when an arrangement is created, activated and closed.

The EV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT application is used to capture the requirement of the evidence. The categories of the requirements are created in EV.REQUIREMENT.CATEGORY (virtual table). When the lessee fails to meet the required conditions, the bank can take necessary actions against the lessee. In asset finance, the consequences are mapped to the AA.ACTION record in RESTRICT.ACTIVATION , for which the ASSET.FINANCE-ACTIVATE-ARRANGEMENT activity type is configured in the Activity property class.


##### ConfiguringAA.CLASS.DEFINITION

The AA.CLASS.DEFINITION application holds the evidence template required by the financial institution. For example, the financial institution acquires the asset (car) and creates an arrangement. Each asset is differentiated by the model number, manufacturer, vehicle registration number, engine number and chassis number. These data are captured in AA.CLASS.DEFINITION under the template required by the financial institution as shown below.


##### ConfiguringEV.DES.

The system creates a record for the evidence condition in the EV.DES. .


##### ConfiguringAA.DEFINITION.MANAGER

The user can publish the record of evidence in the AA.DEFINITION.MANAGER application by setting the Class Type field as EVIDENCE.CLASS and Publish Status field as COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY, after the record is published, as shown in the below screenshot.


##### ConfiguringEV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT

The EV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT application holds all the records required for the arrangement to fulfil the evidence. When the arrangement is created, the customer’s Debt Service Ratio must be entered, based on the financial statement to proceed further with compliance.

> **⚠️ Note:** Each financial institution has its own debt service ratio grid.

When the arrangement is activated, the primary customer must accept the Certificate of Acceptance, which contains all the details of the vehicle or a machinery on which the customer and bank agree, to create the asset finance arrangement.

In the above screenshot, the evidence is submitted based on the Event or Periodic (at any frequency) based on the requirement of the bank.


##### Using Evidence Property Class in Asset Finance

The Evidence property class plays a significant role in the Asset Finance module. Mandatory documents are maintained and tracked using the Evidence property class. The inspection of the asset and its insurance renewal must be tracked on a periodic basis. The mandatory documents can be set as a condition when the contract is activated and the same can be stopped by defining it in the Consequence field.

In the Asset Finance module, the Covenant tab implies that the lessee or primary customer must submit the mandatory set of documents when the arrangement is created. The frequency and when it is due are defined in each evidence in the covenant. The Notice Days attribute is set to 15D indicating that the system raises a notice 15 days prior to the actual due date of the evidence.

The Condition tab holds the rule that the lessee or primary customer must accept the Certificate of Acceptance before the arrangement is activated. If the lessee or primary customer fails to submit the Certificate of Acceptance, the activation of arrangement is blocked as defined in the Consequence attribute.


##### Defining Forward Dated Evidence

The forward dating type can be added to the evidence property which is attached to the asset product. The Evidence condition, which needs to be in effect (at present and future) can be added after creating the arrangement at a later date.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Evidence property class is used to track and maintain the documents to be collected from the customer. The Evidence property class is defined by covenants and conditions. The covenants conditions are type of conditions that are set by the lessor while availing the credit (for example, finance or operating lease), which the lessee needs to adhere to.

Refer the Evidence section for more information on Evidence property class.

The asset finance arrangement is established for the primary customer with the evidence condition as shown in the screenshot below.

This condition indicates that the certificate of acceptance for the vehicle needs to be completed before the asset finance arrangement is activated. Otherwise, the system restricts the activation of the arrangement.

When the ASSET.FINANCE-ACTIVATE-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered to activate the arrangement without completing the condition as defined in the evidence property condition, the system raises the “Covenants/Conditions not met for the Activity” validation error.

The lessee completes the certificate of acceptance for the vehicle as shown in the screenshot below.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Process Method attribute is set as Online in the EV.EVIDENCE application, after completing the evidence, the process is completed online. But, if it is set as Service, then the service EV.EVIDENCE.STATUS.SERVICE must be run to complete the process.

After submitting the evidence, the lessee triggers the ASSET.FINANCE-ACTIVATE-ARRANGEMENT activity to activate the asset finance arrangement.


#### 📋 Tasks

The covenants and conditions functionality is a guarantee that needs to be honoured by the counterparty or lessee to activate and continue the asset finance agreement. The customer must submit the covenant, which is validated on an agreed frequency. A condition is validated when activating the arrangement.

### 3.9  Creating Arrangement


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This section explains about the creation of arrangement in asset finance products.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.PRODUCT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Asset Reference*, *Cancel Period*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Customer Role*, *Effective Date* ... +7 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This section explains about the creation of arrangement in asset finance products.

1. Create New Arrangement – Capture basic details like customer ID, currency, agreement term, asset price or finance amount, pricing (interest rate and charges), and other terms and conditions that are required to create a new asset finance arrangement. Apart from this, Asset reference maintained in the Fixed Assets module is mandatory at the arrangement creation level.
2. Activate Arrangement – Use an activity to activate the arrangement. This activity marks the asset(s) is/are delivered and accepted by the client (that is, Asset Status to “Leased-Out”) and initiates collecting the lease payments (Rentals) as either “Arrears” or “Advance” as per the agreed rental plan. Evidence Conditions (Conditions Precedent) can be used to collect “Certificate of Acceptance” as document evidence and pre-condition for initiating activation.

On the commencement of an Asset Finance arrangement, finance amount, agreement term, and schedule of repayment are decided and agreed between the parties (for example, lessee, lessor, and/or dealer). The schedule of payment which is referred as rental is calculated based on two factors:

- Initial deposit amount or down payment.
- Estimate future residual value of the asset.

The arrangement activation can be delayed due to non-payment of initial deposit or some other reasons. In such cases, the arrangement is automatically cancelled when the cancellation period is reached.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Create the Asset Finance arrangement under the ASSET.FINANCE product line and they are currency specific with the reverse and replay functionality using AA Framework.

The asset finance products are grouped into either contract hire, finance lease or hire purchase based on their common characteristics. The user can define these product groups and can create different products under these groups as per their business need.


##### Configuring Account

Based on the Lease Type attribute in Account property class, the Asset Finance arrangements are classified into finance lease, operating lease or hire purchase. While creating the arrangement, the Lease Type attribute is automatically updated as:

- ‘Finance’ for finance lease and hire purchase arrangements.
- ‘Operating’ for operating lease arrangements.

The arrangement related information is also reflected in AA.ARRANGEMENT application. On the commencement of an Asset Finance arrangement,

- Asset Reference attribute captures the asset ID.
- Lease Type attribute captures the type of asset finance arrangement.


##### Configuring Commitment and Term

Term Amount property class defines the finance amount, agreement term or maturity date and cancel period of the arrangement. On the commencement of an Asset Finance arrangement,

- Amount attribute captures the finance amount and capital cost in acquiring the asset.
- Term attribute captures the agreement term, it can be entered as number of days (D), weeks (W), months (M) or years (Y).
- Maturity Date attribute captures the agreement maturity date. If the Maturity Date is specified then the value in the Term attribute is calculated by the system in days (D) format.
- Cancel Period attribute captures the automatic cancellation period, it can be entered as number of days (D), weeks (W), months (M) or years (Y). The cancellation date is calculated as New Arrangement activity effective date + Cancel Period (inclusive) and arrangement is cancelled on mentioned date if it is not activated. For example, if the arrangement creation date is 10 Feb, 2023 and the cancel period is set as 7D, then the arrangement is automatically cancelled if the customer is not activating the arrangement by 17 Feb 2023.
- Maturity Type attribute indicates the system to default the maturity date as final payment date based on the No of payments attribute defined in the repayment schedule. Select the Maturity Type attribute as Payment.end.date, additionally Term and Maturity Date attributes must be left blank.


##### Configuring Schedule

Payment Schedule property class defines the schedule of payments. On the commencement of an Asset Finance arrangement, the Payment Type attribute captures the repayment profile from the dropdown list.

Read the Payment Schedule property class for more information on payment schedule definition for Asset Finance.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the steps involved in creating an Asset Finance arrangement.


##### Creating an Arrangement

The ASSET.FINANCE-NEW-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered to create a new asset finance arrangement. To create a new arrangement, set the below attributes in the ASSET.FINANCE-NEW-ARRANGEMENT activity.

- Customer and Customer Role : Enter the details of multiple customers with different roles. Read the Customer property class User Guide for more information.
- Product : Enter a valid product ID in AA.PRODUCT available for the corresponding branch.
- Currency : Validate the currency entered for the arrangement with the existing currencies of the product.
- Effective Date : Validate if the selected effective date is on or after the product availability date.

In addition, provide the asset reference, finance amount, term or maturity date and payment schedule option.

To create a new asset finance arrangement,

1. Business Banking Operations and click Product Catalog .
2. In the Asset Finance Product Groups section, click the required product groups.
3. In the Finance Lease Products section, click the icon of the corresponding product to display the Arrangement Creation screen.
4. Enter the customer information along with currency, effective date.
5. Validate the arrangement, to enable the below mentioned sections. Select a value in the Asset Reference attribute in the Account section. Enter a value in the Finance Amount and Term attributes in the Commitment and Term section. Select a value in the Payment Type attribute in the Under Schedule section Commit and authorise the asset finance arrangement to generate the arrangement ID.

Authorise the created arrangements to generate the following accounting entries for the new arrangement activity.

The contract wise balances (EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES.BALANCE) enquiry displays the accounting entries of an asset finance arrangement after creation.


##### Activating an Arrangement

The ASSET.FINANCE-ACTIVATE-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered to activate a new asset finance arrangement. To activate an asset finance arrangement,

1. Asset Finance Transactions and click Find Arrangement .
2. In the Find Arrangement enquiry, click Authorised Tab and enter the Arrangement ID in arrangement search criteria and click Find button.
3. In the Find Arrangement enquiry, click the Overview icon corresponding to the selected arrangement.
4. In the Overview composite screen, click the New Activity link on the top corner.
5. In the New Activities enquiry, click the Do Activity Today link corresponding to the activate arrangement activity to display the Activate Arrangement dialog box.
6. Commit and authorise the activate arrangement activity to change the arrangement status to Current.

Authorise the activated arrangements to generate the following accounting entries for activating the activity depending on the value in the Lease Type attribute.

For Lease Type as Finance,

Once the agreement is activated, the CUR is debited and the amount is credited to the FASUSPENSE account. The balance in FASUSPENSE is settled for an asset in fixed asset system and it initiates the payment to the supplier if the amount is not paid.

The Contract wise balances (EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES.BALANCE) enquiry displays the accounting entries of an asset finance arrangement after creation.

For Lease Type as Operating,

There are no balance movements from arrangement to fixed asset system as the asset remains in the balance sheet and starts depreciation. The fixed asset system initiates the payment to supplier if not paid already.

The Contract wise balances (EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES.BALANCE) enquiry displays the accounting entries of an asset finance arrangement after creation.


##### Cancelling an Arrangement

The ASSET.FINANCE-CANCEL-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered to cancel a new asset finance arrangement. This activity can be triggered by user to cancel manually or system triggers automatically on a cancellation date.

To cancel an asset finance arrangement manually,

1. Asset Finance Transactions and click Find Arrangement .
2. In the Find Arrangement enquiry, click Unauthorised Tab and enter the Arrangement ID in Arrangement search criteria and then click on the Find button.
3. In the Find Arrangement enquiry, click on Overview icon corresponding to the selected arrangement.
4. In the Overview composite screen, click the New Activity link on the top corner.
5. In the New Activities enquiry, click Do Activity Today corresponding to the Cancel Arrangement activity.
6. The Cancel Arrangement dialog box appears.
7. Commit and authorise the cancel arrangement activity.

To cancel an asset finance arrangement automatically,

1. Create an arrangement on 12th April and set the Cancel Period attribute to 4D.
2. If the arrangement is not activated by 16th April, then the system triggers the cancel arrangement activity on 16th April.

| Contract Start Date | Term Amount | Term | Interest | Advance | Payment Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16-Apr-2025 | USD 25,000.00 | 1Y | 4.50% | 10.00% | Monthly |

Authorise the created arrangements to generate the following accounting entries to cancel the activity and to reverse the commitment balance.


#### 📋 Tasks

Asset Finance module in transact allows the financial institution to book an asset finance arrangement. Arrangement can be created in different currencies and the complete life cycle of an asset finance agreement with creation, activation, billing, settlement, maintenance, and closure is embedded in the Asset Finance module. It supports a wide range of asset finance product features with configurable conditions.

#### 📖 Introduction

The ASSET.FINANCE product line supports the addition of the Limit property class to the asset finance products.

The credit limit structure can be created in the LIMIT application and linked to the asset finance arrangement using the Limit property. Collaterals can be linked to the credit limit using the COLLATERAL and COLLATERL.RIGHT applications.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Limit Parameter and Limit product are setup in the system to create the Limit for the Lessee.

Read Configuring Limit Products Creation for more information on the configuration of LIMIT.PARAMATER and LIMIT.REFERENCE , and Limits module for more information on the LIMIT application.


##### Limit Property Class

The Limit property class is not a mandatory PC in the ASSET.FINANCE Product Line. The bank or financial institution (FI) can include the LIMIT property in AA.PRODUCT.GROUP and the AA Products for the business expectation.

The Limit created for the customer or lessee is linked to the asset finance arrangement using the Limit PC.

Read the Arrangement Architecture module for more information on the product configurations.

Read Limit for more information on the Limit property class functionality.

##### Limit

The Limit created for the Lessee is attached in the Limit ID attribute in the Limit condition.

Read Creating Arrangement for more information on creating the Asset Finance arrangement.

The screenshot below shows the limit allocation percentage of the Lessee as 100%.

When the user needs to update the Limit ID in the Asset Finance arrangement, the ASSET.FINANCE-UPDATE-LIMIT activity can be triggered to update the Limit ID.

If the user requires to update the Limit of Lessee in the arrangement, the user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-UPDATE-LIMIT activity from the New Activity option in the Overview screen and authorise the activity.

The user can view the updated limit of the arrangement in the section Limit/Collateral Details section in the Arrangement Overview screen.

### 3.11  Early payoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Early payoff allows the lessee to settle all the outstanding balances before the end of the agreed term. The calculated payoff amount includes unbilled principal and interests excluding the rebates if any, billed regular payments, subscription payments, fees or charges, tax. Upon settling the payoff...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adv Payment Type*, *Adv Type Value*, *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Arrangement ID*, *Asset Reference*, *Context Name*, *Context Value* ... +14 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Early payoff allows the lessee to settle all the outstanding balances before the end of the agreed term. The calculated payoff amount includes unbilled principal and interests excluding the rebates if any, billed regular payments, subscription payments, fees or charges, tax. Upon settling the payoff quotation, the system closes the asset finance arrangement and dispose the asset to the lessee.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section helps the user to configure the required attribute in the Payoff property class:

In the Payoff product condition, the user must define the Payoff Settlement attribute as ‘Full’ to perform the Early Payoff in the contract.

The user can define the expiry in number of days for the payoff quotation in the Expiry Days attribute. The system expires the payoff quotation from the payoff date based on the number days defined in the Expiry Days attribute. The user can settle the payoff statement for the quoted payoff amount before the payoff statement’s expiry date.


#### 🔧 Working With

By configuring the payoff condition with the Payoff Settlement attribute as Full, the user can perform the early payoff in a contract to settle all the outstanding balances and bills.


##### Calculating Payoff

The user can trigger the Early Payoff only in the active contract. Upon triggering ASSET.FINANCE-CALCULATE-PAYOFF, the system generates the payoff quotation or statement (Info bill). The payoff statement quotes the outstanding principal, interest, rebate on interest, due and overdue balances.

Upon settling the payoff statement, the system moves the contract status to pending closure, and the asset is disposed to the lessee.

### 3.12  ExtendTerm


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Asset Finance, the arrangement can be extended to the secondary term at the end of the contract term. The user can choose the maturity options such as Extend the Agreement and Extend and Return in the Asset Finance arrangement.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Advance Payment Type*, *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Arrangement ID*, *Asset Reference*, *Change Date Type*, *Change Period*, *Currency* ... +12 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In Asset Finance, the arrangement can be extended to the secondary term at the end of the contract term. The user can choose the maturity options such as Extend the Agreement and Extend and Return in the Asset Finance arrangement.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In the Term Amount property class, the user can choose from the following extend term options in the On Maturity attribute

> **⚠️ Note:** The lessee can extend the contract only once with the below options.

- Extend The Agreement – The system extends the arrangement into the secondary term at the time of maturity. The lessee can purchase the asset by paying the residual amount at the end of the arrangement's extended or secondary term only for contracts of the finance lease-type and not for operating lease-type.
- Extend And Return - The system extends the arrangement into the secondary term at the time of maturity. The lessee can return the asset to the lessor at the end of the arrangement's secondary or extended term.


##### Extending Term Period

The Change Product PC is configured to define the period of the secondary term. The Change Date Type attribute can be defined only as a period, and the secondary term can be defined in the Change Period attribute.


#### 🔧 Working With

The secondary term for the asset finance arrangement can be defined as Extend The Agreement or Extend And Return using the On Maturity attribute in the Term Amount property class.


##### Schedule for Extended Term

The user can define the schedule for the extended or secondary term as a future dated arrangement condition while creating a new asset finance arrangement. In order to define the future dated schedule condition for the secondary or extended term in the new arrangement activity, the user needs to input the arrangement's term in the Term attribute of the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY. The system defaults this term in the Term attribute of the Term Amount property class.


##### Extend The Agreement

The Extend the Agreement option denotes that the Lessee agrees to extend the arrangement's term for the residual amount. The base amount for the secondary term can be a part of or the entire residual amount, that is, the residual amount can be defined for the secondary term using the forward dated schedule condition . The lessee can purchase the asset by settling the residual amount, if any, during the secondary term of the arrangement. The lessee can purchase the asset only in the Finance Lease type of asset finance arrangement. Read the Introduction to Residual section for more information on residuals in Asset Finance.

| Term | Residual Amount | Guaranteed Residual Amount | Period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary Term | USD 5,000 | USD 4,000 | 1 Year |
| Secondary Term |  |  | 6 Months |

| Term | Residual Amount | Period |
|---|---|---|
| Primary Term | USD 10000 | 1 Year |
| Secondary Term | - | 6 Months |


##### Extend And Return

In asset finance, Extend and Return denotes that the lessee can extend the secondary term for the residual amount described in the contract. The lessee has an option to extend the contract for a part of or the entire residual amount. The lessee must return the asset by the end of the secondary term.

| Term | Residual Amount | Guaranteed Residual Amount | Period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary Term | USD 10,000 | USD 5000 | 1 Year |
| Secondary Term | USD 5000 | USD 4,000 | 6 Months |

| Term | Residual Amount | Period |
|---|---|---|
| Primary Term | USD 20000 | 1 Year |
| Secondary Term | USD 10000 | 6 Months |

### 3.13  IFRS 16 Regulations


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This section provides a brief explanation about IFRS Regulations.*
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.CASHFLOW`, `IFRS.ACCT.METHODS`, `IFRS.PARAMETER`, `IFRS.POSTING.DETAILS`, `IFRS.SUB.TYPE`, `PV.MANAGEMENT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account Type*, *Asset Type*, *Default Recalc Method*, *IFRS Classification*, *NPV Method*, *NPV Rate*, *Posting Required*, *Posting Style* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This section provides a brief explanation about IFRS Regulations.

IFRS 16 is an accounting standard issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) that outlines the procedures to recognise, measure, and disclose lease agreements in the balance sheet.

REPORTING property class feature in asset finance enables banks and financial institutions to report the hire purchase and lease agreements according to IFRS 16 regulation standards from a lessor perspective.

This ensures adherence to the accounting treatment for the events (listed below) that affect the financials of lease agreements and the underlying financed assets.

- Initial Contract
- Upfront Payments / Deposits
- Contract Maturity
- Mid-life amendments that could affect the future cashflow
- Impairment losses (if any)
