### 3.14  Interest


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The interest rate for Asset Finance arrangements is mostly calculated using a fixed interest rate. Periodic rates, such as EURIBOR and floating rates are also used. For periodic and floating rate types, a margin may be applied. Interest rate is calculated using the flat interest rate or reducing bal...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUAL.HIST`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.PARAMETER`, `AA.PROPERTY`, `BASIC.INTEREST`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accounting Mode*, *Archive Period*, *Compounding Type*, *Custom Name*, *Custom Rate*, *Custom Rate Calc*, *Custom Type*, *Custom Value* ... +7 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The interest rate for Asset Finance arrangements is mostly calculated using a fixed interest rate. Periodic rates, such as EURIBOR and floating rates are also used. For periodic and floating rate types, a margin may be applied. Interest rate is calculated using the flat interest rate or reducing balance rate method. Interest amount is calculated upfront and accounted as an interest receivable element.

Asset Finance arrangements support multiple interest rates such as the lease interest, margin and penalty rates. The margin rate is the rate that the financial institution gains out of the specific arrangement. The penalty interest can be calculated based on the overdue balances.

The following methods can be used to calculate interest:

- Flat rate basis - The interest rate is applied on the principal amount throughout the term.
- Reducing rate or Diminishing rate basis - The interest rate is applied on the outstanding principal.
- Flat amount basis - The interest calculation is carried out in an external system and the calculated amount is used as the total interest for the Asset Finance arrangement.

In a hire purchase and a finance lease, the calculated repayment amount received from the lessee is split into the principal and the interest components. The interest portion is accounted as the profit.

In an operating lease, the calculated repayment amount received from the lessee is recognised as income to the bank.

The rate change advice or correspondence with the new interest rate and payment amount can be sent to the customer in advance based on the configurations.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details about configuring the accounting entries and interest types in Asset Finance.


##### Configuring Accounting Entries

The following section describes the Receivable Accounting and Principal Receivable options in detail.

The Type attribute is used to define the property type in the AA.PROPERTY application is configured as ‘Receivable Accounting’ in the Interest property configured for Asset Finance products. This is to indicate that the interest is calculated upfront and accounted as Receivable. As this is configured at the property level, the Accounting Mode attribute in the Interest property condition is updated as ‘Receivable’ at the arrangement creation level.

The Asset Finance arrangements support multiple interest configurations. The Property Type in AA.PROPERTY application is configured as ‘Principal Receivable’ to indicate that the Interest property is part of the multiple interest.

> **⚠️ Note:** Only one Interest property in a product can be defined as ‘Principal Receivable’ type. The system validates this at the product proofing level, and at the arrangement creation level.

The Rate Type attribute in the Interest property class is used to configure the interest type as either a flat rate, a reducing rate, or a flat amount. The asset finance arrangements support these three rate types. The Rate Type attribute can be input at the arrangement creation level.


##### Configuring Interest

The following section describes about configuring floating rates, periodic rates, custom rates, archival of interests, defining phase based interest conditions and more.

When a backdated floating interest index key (that is, from the BASIC.INTEREST application) is changed, the system triggers the change interest activity to change the interest accordingly. As the rate change is backdated, the system performs a reverse and replay of all the activities associated with the rate change date for all the underlying arrangements. The replay function then applies the new interest rate specified and recalculates the accrued interest accordingly.

The periodic index key is linked to the variable rates based on the specific period (that is, PERIODIC.INTEREST). Once the arrangement is active, the periodic rate is fixed until the periodic rate is reset by the system. The system automatically resets the periodic rates using the ASSET.FINANCE-PERIODIC.RESET-LEASEINT activity based on the periodic reset frequency configured in the Periodic Reset attribute in the Interest property condition.

The custom rate is a type of source rate calculation in the Interest Property Class. By setting the Custom Rate attribute to Yes, the custom rate calculation can be enabled. The user must add an API to the Custom Rate Calc field to facilitate the calculation. To configure custom values for the API, the user can use the attributes such as Custom Type , Custom Name , and Custom Value .

The system invokes the CUSTOM RATE CALC AP during:

- Change interest activity by the core interest processing module
- Accrual or capitalisation or make-due processing, resulting in the interest rate to be derived dynamically

The Runtime Rate Calc attribute controls the run time calculation if it is set to Yes,

The system provides an option to define different interest rates for a product. The rate can be different at various stages of the life cycle of the product, based on the requirement of the financial institutions. The financial institution can set up interest rates by configuring the Effective Phase attribute in the Product Phases tab of the Product Designer. Read Product Designer (temenos.com) for more information.

The system supports compounding of both debit and credit interest. Compounding interest applies a factor to the compound interest calculation based on the number of compounding periods in the year. This field defines the number of compounding periods that are applicable. The Compounding Type attribute provides a factor in the calculation of the interest amount only. It does not actually affect the base principal amount, that is, the calculated interest amount is exclusive of the principal amount.

The interest accrual values (Period Start and Period End set of values with their corresponding From Date and To Date set of values) in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS application can be archived and stored in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUAL.HIST table to improve the performance of the system. To achieve this, the user needs to set Archive Period and Retain Period attributes in the AA.PARAMETER application .

Read Archival of Interest Accruals for more information on the archival processing of interest accruals.

Asset Finance supports Rate Cards (Pricing Grids product line) for defining interest definitions. Read Rate Grid and Margin Grid for more information on Rate and Margin Grids.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Asset Finance arrangements can be created with different interest types like fixed, periodic index or floating rate. The interest can be calculated using the flat rate method or as a reducing rate. The interest can also be defined as a flat amount. The Rate Type attribute in the Interest property condition is used to differentiate the rate type at the arrangement creation level.

The user (BBOFFICER) can input the rate type to be used for a particular Asset Finance arrangement. If the Rate Type attribute is chosen as FLAT.AMOUNT value, then input in the Flat Amount attribute becomes mandatory.


##### Calculating Interest Accrual

The interest for the Asset Finance arrangements is calculated upfront and accounted as Receivable at the commencement of the arrangement. The calculation of interest accrual differs based on the classification of the Asset Finance arrangement.

- For a finance lease, the interest portion is accrued on a daily basis by applying the interest rate on the reducing principal amount. The interest portion of the finance lease arrangement is accounted as an income to the bank.
- For an operating lease, the entire repayment amount is accounted as a profit. The interest is calculated upfront and accrued on a straight-line basis. The interest accrual is calculated by dividing the repayment amount by the number of days in the payment period.

The system raises info entries for the principal and interest portions as LEASEPRINCIPALINF and LEASEINTINF. The real entry is raised for a single balance as LEASEINT upon generating the due bill, which is accounted as an income to the bank.

For an operating lease, the values for raising the real entry are updated in the AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS application with a different ID format containing --REC. This information is used for raising the bill and updating the ECB balances for the operating lease arrangements.

The record in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS for the arrangement is updated with due amount as null.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for the Interest on Asset Finance feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for the Interest on Asset Finance feature.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUAL.HIST`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.PARAMETER`, `AA.PROPERTY`, `BASIC.INTEREST`

### 3.15  Interest Rebate


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Interest rebate allows the lessor to provide a various method of rebate on future interest for early payoff or Early or Forced termination.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Rebate Activity*, *Rebate Calc From*, *Rebate Context*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Interest rebate allows the lessor to provide a various method of rebate on future interest for early payoff or Early or Forced termination.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section helps the user to configure the required attributes in the Interest property class:

In the Interest product condition, the Rebate Activity , Rebate Calc From and Rebate Context attributes are available for configuring the interest rebate functionality.

Rebate Activity : Defines the activity for which the interest rebate calculation method to be defined in the Rebate Calc From attribute. The activities being configured in this attribute must belong to ASSET.FINANCE-TERMINATE- ARRANGEMENT or ASSET.FINANCE-CALCULATE-PAYOFF activity classes.

Rebate Calc From : Defines the interest rebate calculated method for the subject interest property.

To calculate the rebate during the payoff or termination for the subject interest property, the following options are available in Rebate Calc From .

- Effective Date: The accrued interest is quoted or billed up to the effective date of the payoff or termination activity. That is, Rebates the interest from effective date up to the payment end date.
- Period End Date: The interest accrual is quoted or billed up to the current interest period end date. That is, Rebates the interest from current interest period end date up to the payment end date.
- Payment End Date: The overall interest accrual up to the payment end date is quoted or billed. That is, no rebate.
- Context: The required interest amount can be passed as the context value to be quoted or billed for the subject interest property.

Rebate Context : Defines the context name for the option Context in the Rebate Calc From attribute. This attribute is mandatory if Rebate Calc From is defined as Context.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can configure rebates for the interest properties to be applied during the early payoff and termination.

### 3.16  Maturity Options


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Asset Finance, the term ‘Maturity Options’ refers to the end- of-term options that opted by the customer beyond the primary period of the finance agreement.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Arrangement ID*, *Asset Reference*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Guaranteed Percentage*, *Guaranteed Residual* ... +12 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In Asset Finance, the term ‘Maturity Options’ refers to the end- of-term options that opted by the customer beyond the primary period of the finance agreement.

- Purchase the Asset – Indicates that the customer has opted to purchase the asset by paying the remaining balance.
- Return the Asset – Indicates that the customer has opted to return the asset at the end.
- Extend The Agreement - Indicates that the customer has opted to extend for secondary period.

Refer the Introduction to Extend Term section for more information on extending the term.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user can choose the maturity options in the On Maturity attribute in the Term Amount property class.

- Purchase The Asset - At the end of the arrangement term, the residual amount becomes due. The lessee can purchase the asset by paying the residual amount at the end of the arrangement term. This option can be used only for the contracts of Finance Lease type and not for Operating Lease type. If the On Maturity field is left blank, the system considers the Purchase The Asset option by default for the contacts of Finance Lease type.
- Return The Asset - The lessee can return the asset to the lessor at the end of the arrangement term.


#### 🔧 Working With

Maturity Options for the asset finance arrangement can be defined as Purchase the Asset (Buyout) or Return the Asset (Repossession) using the On Maturity attribute in the Term Amount property class.


##### Purchase the Asset (Buyout)

In Asset Finance arrangement, the maturity option can be defined as purchase the asset (buyout) for the lessee to purchase the asset. In this case, the residual amount is billed during the maturity of the arrangement. The lessee settles all the outstanding bills to purchase the asset.

The maturity option is defined as Purchase the Asset for the asset finance arrangement with commitment amount USD 25,000.

The Residual amount is defined as USD 5,000 and the Guaranteed Residual is defined as USD 4,500.


###### Billing

The system makes the residual amount due during the maturity of the asset finance arrangement.


###### Overdue

The Residual Amount bill undergoes overdue processing if the bill is not settled. Read Configuring Billing or Invoicing section for more information on overdue process in asset finance.


###### Settlement

The residual bill component in the final bill must be settled using the repayment activities like the other due bills. Upon settling all the Residual Bill component, if there are no other due or overdue balance, the system moves the arrangement to the Pending Closure status.


##### Return the Asset (Repossession)

The maturity option ‘Return the Asset’ denotes that the Lessee must return the asset by the end of the arrangement's term.

During the maturity, the system moves the residual amount from CURLEASEPRINCIPAL to RESLEASEPRINCIPAL.

After the maturity of the arrangement, the user needs to manually trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-REPOSSESS.ASSET-ARRANGEMENT repossession activity and pass the current market value of the asset in the Txn Amount attribute, for the system to compare the market value against the residual amount and the guaranteed residual to raise the appropriate accounting entries.

Following are the illustrations for Finance Lease:

| Residual Amount | Guaranteed Residual Amount | Market Value |
|---|---|---|
| USD 5,000 | USD 4,000 | USD 7,000 |

| Residual Amount | Guaranteed Residual Amount | Market Value |
|---|---|---|
| USD 5,000 | USD 4,000 | USD 4,500 |

| Residual Amount | Guaranteed Residual Amount | Market Value |
|---|---|---|
| USD 5,000 | USD 4,000 | USD 3,500 |

In the Operating Lease type arrangements, the system moves the residual balance from CURLEASEPRINCIPALINF to RESLEASEPRINCIPALINF balance type during the maturity.

During the Repossession activity ASSET.FINANCE-REPOSSESS.ASSET-ARRANGEMENT, the system raises the self-balancing entry to nullify the residual balance in RESLEASEPRINCIPALINF balance type.

The maturity option is defined as Return the Asset for the asset finance arrangement with commitment amount USD 1,00,000.

The Residual amount is defined as USD 10,000.

Upon triggering the repossession activity, market value is not considered to settle the balance in RESLEASEPRINCIPALINF. The system raises the self balance entry to nullify RESLEASEPRINCIPALINF balance.

Upon settling all the Bill components, if there are no other due or overdue balance, the system moves the arrangement to the Pending Closure status.


#### 📋 Tasks

Maturity options refer to the choices for the lessee to do with the asset at the end of term or during the maturity of the asset finance arrangement.

In Maturity Options, the user can perform the following activities:

Residual Amount / Residual Percentage Guaranteed Residual / Guaranteed Percentage Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. Accept the overrides, if any. |

| Overview Screen | Click the Overview icon. |

### 3.17  Midlife Amendments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The midlife amendment feature allows the users to change the payment schedule, customer or party, term and finance amount, and the interest rate in the asset finance arrangement.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`, `BASIC.INTEREST`, `PERIODIC.INTEREST`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Change Amount*, *Customer*, *Customer Role*, *Fixed Rate*, *Payment Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The midlife amendment feature allows the users to change the payment schedule, customer or party, term and finance amount, and the interest rate in the asset finance arrangement.


##### Changing Payment Frequency

The user can change the payment frequency to be effective from the current, past, and future dates in the arrangement. For example, if a user has already set an arrangement with monthly payment, and needs to change it to quarterly payment during the lifecycle of the arrangement, the system recalculates the payments or the term, based on the user’s recalculation setup in the Payment Schedule property condition. In addition, the user can also generate the appropriate pre-notices or advice for the payment frequency change based on the configurations in the Activity Messaging property conditions.


##### Changing the Ownership

The user can change the parties involved in the arrangement to be effective from the current, past, and future dates in the arrangement. For example, a user has already set the beneficial owner (lessee) of the asset finance arrangement. Now, the user can add or remove the involved parties from the asset finance arrangement. The user can also generate the appropriate pre-notices or advice for the party amendment based on the configurations in the Activity Messaging property conditions.


##### Changing the Finance Amount and Term

The user can change the finance commitment amount and the term of the arrangement and make it effective from the current, past, and future dates in the arrangement.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user cannot change the finance amount in an activated arrangement.

When the user changes the finance amount, the system recalculates the scheduled payment amount or term based on the recalculation configuration in the Payment Schedule property condition. The user can generate the appropriate pre-notices or advice for the change in the finance amount based on the configurations in the Activity Messaging property conditions.


##### Changing the Interest Rate

The type of interest rate can be fixed, variable, or periodic for an asset finance arrangement. The system supports the rate changes during the lifecycle of the arrangement for finance and operating type agreements.

The user can change the interest rates to be effective from the current, past, and future dates in the arrangement. The rate change requires recalculation of the scheduled payment amount. The system recalculates the payments or the term, based on the recalculation setup in the Payment Schedule condition. The user can generate the appropriate pre-notices or advice correspondence for the change in the finance amount based on the configurations in the Activity Messaging property conditions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the configurations required to change the payment schedule, customer or party, term and finance amount, and the interest rate in the asset finance arrangement.


##### Changing the Payment Frequency

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-SCHEDULE activity using the New Activity option in the AA overview screen to change the payment frequency of the arrangement. The user can trigger the activity to be effective from the current, past, and future date in the arrangement.

Refer Payment Schedule for more information on the Payment Schedule property condition.

The user can configure the payment types such as CONSTANT, PRINCIPAL, and INTEREST.ONLY with the required payment frequencies in the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application.

For example, if the user configures the payment type as CONSTANT.MONTHLY in the Payment Schedule condition, the CONSTANT Payment Type follows the monthly payment frequency.

The payment frequency amendments result in the recalculation of payment or term based on the configuration in the Payment Schedule property condition.


###### Recalculation of Payment Frequency

The user can configure the below fields in the Payment Schedule condition for automatic recalculation of the payment schedule.

- On Activity - Holds the list of activities that require automatic recalculation.
- Recalculate - Indicates the recalculation type for respective activities the user configures in the On Activity attribute.

If the user wants to recalculate the payment amount, the user must configure the 'Payment' option in the Payment Schedule property condition. For term recalculation, the user should configure the option 'Term' in the Recalculate attribute.

Refer Schedule of Payments for more information on Payment Schedule property condition.

Refer Working with Page for more information on the working illustrations and Activity Messaging for more information on how the system sends the pre-notice or advice or correspondence to the end customer using the Activity Messaging property class.


##### Changing the Ownership

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-CUSTOMER activity to change the ownership (that is, lessee) of the arrangement. The user must change the primary party in the Customer and Customer Role attributes while validating the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-CUSTOMER activity. The user can trigger this activity to be effective from current, past, and future dates in the arrangement.

Also, the user can update the Customer property conditions at the arrangement level using the ASSET.FINANCE-UPDATE-CUSTOMER activity to update the tax, limit liabilities for the parties. The user can configure the below attributes in the Customer property condition to maintain the primary party details.

- Customer – Maintains the party references involving in the asset finance arrangement.
- Customer Role – Maintains the relevant roles of the parties, that is, lessee and supplier and so on.

Refer Customer for more information on the Customer property class and the Working with Page for the working illustrations.

Refer Activity Messaging for more information on the pre-notice or advice or correspondence to be sent to the end customer using the Activity Messaging property class.


##### Changing the Finance Amount and Term

The user can change the finance amount of the asset finance arrangement during the lifecycle of the arrangement. The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-INCREASE-LEASECOMMITMENT or ASSET.FINANCE-DECREASE-LEASECOMMITMENT activity as per the business expectation to increase or decrease the finance amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user cannot change the finance amount in the activated arrangement.

The Amount attribute holds the initially committed finance amount. The Change Amount attribute under Term Amount property condition can be input by triggering the INCREASE or DECREASE activities. The Change Amount attribute represents the amount to increase or decrease on the original finance amount.

The periodic index key is linked to the variable rates based on the period of times (that is, PERIODIC.INTEREST ). Once the arrangement is active, the periodic rate is fixed until the periodic rate is reset by the system. The system automatically resets the periodic rates using the ASSET.FINANCE-PERIODIC.RESET-LEASEINT activity, based on the periodic reset frequency configured in the Periodic Reset attribute in the Interest property condition.

> **⚠️ Note:** For INCREASE activity, the amount must be a positive value (greater than zero). For DECREASE activity, the amount must be a negative value (lesser than zero).

Refer Term Amount for more information on the Term Amount property class.


###### Changing the Term

The user can change the term of the asset finance arrangement during the lifecycle of the arrangement. The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE.TERM-LEASECOMMITMENT activity to change the term of the arrangement.

The user can change the Term or Maturity Date attribute in the Term Amount property condition to trigger the CHANGE.TERM activity. The Term attribute is entered as number of days (D), weeks (W), months (M), or years (Y). If the user changes the value in the Maturity Date attribute, the system recalculates the value in the Term attribute in days format.


###### Recalculation of Finance Amount and Term

For INCREASE or DECREASE commitment actions for increasing or decreasing the finance amount and term, the outstanding principal changes upon changing the finance amount of the arrangement. So, the system recalculates either the payment or the term based on the recalculation configuration in the Payment Schedule property condition.

Refer recalculation in the Configuration page for more information on recalculation configuration in the Payment Schedule property condition and the Working with page for more information on the working illustrations of changing the finance amount.


##### Changing Interest Rate

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-LEASEINT activity to change the interest rate in the Interest property conditions during the lifecycle of an arrangement. The user can trigger this activity to be effective from the current, past, and future dates in the arrangement.


###### Changing Fixed Rate

The user enters the fixed rate directly in Interest property condition. The rate is fixed and does not change like the variable rates automatically. The user can configure the fixed rate in the product or input the fixed rate while creating the arrangement.


###### Changing Variable Rate and Margin

The floating index key is linked to a variable base rate for the floating interest rate (that is, BASIC.INTEREST ). The system uses the currency specific rate from the floating index key for the interest calculation. The user can use margins to adjust the specified rate of interest and to reflect any rate profit realised.


###### Changing Periodic Rate

The periodic index key is linked to the variable rates based on the period of times (that is, PERIODIC.INTEREST). Once the arrangement is active, the periodic rate is fixed until the periodic rate is reset by the system. The system automatically resets the periodic rates using the ASSET.FINANCE-PERIODIC.RESET-LEASEINT activity, based on the periodic reset frequency configured in the Periodic Reset attribute in the Interest property condition.


###### Recalculation of Interest Rate

The rate change amendments result in the recalculation of the payment or the term based on the configuration in the Payment Schedule property condition.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section elaborates on how to work with the midlife amendments feature for changing the payment schedule, customer or party, term and finance amount, and the interest rate in the asset finance arrangement.


##### Changing the Payment Frequency

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-SCHEDULE activity to change the payment frequency in the Payment Schedule property condition during the lifecycle of the arrangement. The user can trigger the activity to be effective from the current, past, and future date in the arrangement.

If the asset finance arrangement for the finance amount of USD 10,000 and one year term is configured as CONSTANT-MONTHLY payment.

The system calculates the current payment amount USD 851.56 based on the new payment frequency.

The financial institution wants the system to recalculate the payment amount post the payment frequency amendments. The user configures the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-SCHEDULE activity in On Activity attribute and configures the option as Payment in the Recalculate attribute in the Payment Schedule property condition.

The schedule projection of the arrangement from the overview screen is shown below.

Now, the user wants to change the frequency to quarterly. So, the user initiates the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-SCHEDULE activity and changes the frequency to quarterly in the Payment Schedule property condition.

The user has to authorise the change for amending the payment frequency to confirm the changes.

Upon authorisation of the activity, the system recalculates the payment amount as USD 2,554.67 and the term remains the same.


##### Changing the Ownership

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-CUSTOMER activity to change the ownership (that is, lessee) of the arrangement and use the Customer , Customer Role attributes in the validation stage of ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-CUSTOMER activity to change the primary party.

Also, the user can update the Customer property conditions at the arrangement level using the activity ASSET.FINANCE-UPDATE-CUSTOMER to update the tax and limit liabilities for the parties. The user can then trigger the activity to be effective from the current, past, and future date in the arrangement.

For example, the lessee of the given asset finance arrangement is '100100 - Harry Crisp'.

The financial institution wants to add a dealer to this asset finance arrangement in a specific circumstance based on an agreement with the subject parties.

The user triggers the activity ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-CUSTOMER and updates the attribute, the part reference number, and the role in the Customer and Customer Role attributes.

The user has to authorise the activity related to the party amendment to confirm the changes.

Upon authorisation of the activity, the system adds the party to the arrangement.


##### Changing the Finance Amount and Term

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-DECREASE-LEASECOMMITMENT or ASSET.FINANCE-DECREASE-LEASECOMMITMENT activity as per the business expectation whether to increase or decrease the finance amount. The Amount attribute holds the initially committed finance amount. The user can input the Change Amount attribute under the Term Amount property condition by triggering the INCREASE or DECREASE activities.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user cannot change the finance amount in an activated arrangement.

The user can trigger the activity to be effective from the current, past, and future date in the arrangement.

For example, the asset finance arrangement is established with the finance amount of USD 8,000 and the term of one year.

The financial institution wants to increase the finance amount by USD 2,000 based on the agreement with the party.

The payment amount of the arrangement is monthly USD 681.23, and the financial summary is as below.

The schedule projection as per the current finance amount and the term from the overview screen is shown below.

The user triggers the ASSET.FINANCE-INCREASE-LEASECOMMITMENT activity and updates the Change Amount attribute with 2000 to increase the finance amount.

The user has to authorise the activity related to the change in the finance amount to confirm the changes.

Upon authorisation of the activity, the system changes the finance amount USD 10,000.

The system recalculates the payment amount of the arrangement as monthly USD 847.91, and the financial summary is as below.

The schedule projection as per the current finance amount and the term from the overview screen is shown below.


##### Changing Interest Rate

The user can trigger the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-LEASEINT activity to change the interest rate such as fixed rate, floating or variable rate key, and margins, in the interest arrangement conditions during the lifecycle of the arrangement. The user can trigger the activity to be effective from the current, past, and future dates in the arrangement.

The system automatically resets the periodic rates using the activity class ASSET.FINANCE-PERIODIC.RESET-LEASEINT based on the periodic reset frequency the user has configured in the Periodic Reset attribute in the Interest property condition.

For example, the asset finance arrangement is established with the finance amount of USD 10,000, the term of one year, and the interest rate of four percentage. The payment frequency is set as monthly.

The payment amount is monthly USD 851.56

The schedule projection and the financial summary of the arrangement from the overview screen is shown below.

The financial institution wants to increase the interest rate from four to five percentage based on the business expectation.

The user triggers the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-LEASEINT activity and change the fixed rate from four to five percentage.

The user has to authorise the activity related to the rate change to confirm the changes.

Upon authorisation of the activity, the system changes the interest rate to five percentage in the asset arrangement.

### 3.18  Migration


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Asset Finance product line supports migration of existing contracts from another system (legacy system) using standard Arrangement Architecture’s (AA) data migration techniques. It enables the banks or financial institutions implementing Temenos Asset Finance solution to migrate the hire purchas...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Asset Finance product line supports migration of existing contracts from another system (legacy system) using standard Arrangement Architecture’s (AA) data migration techniques. It enables the banks or financial institutions implementing Temenos Asset Finance solution to migrate the hire purchase, finance and operating lease agreements from their legacy system into Temenos Asset Finance.

The migration of contracts into Temenos Asset Finance involves migration of the asset’s static and financial data followed by the contract’s static and financial data.


##### Migration of Financed Assets

Read Fixed Asset module for more information on asset migration techniques.


##### Migration of Finance Contracts

The process of migrating contracts into Asset Finance involves the steps below:

1. Take Over Arrangement: Take over of contract’s static data.
2. Capture Balances: Take over of the outstanding balance that is not charged yet and the accrued interest (if any from the last payment date).
3. Capture Bills: Take over of the unpaid bills/invoices that are present and past due.

> **⚠️ Note:** As the situation at each contract is different, depending on each existing contract’s lifecycle stage held in legacy system, step 2 and step 3 above may or may not apply.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

As each implementation is different, depending on the contract’s data in legacy system, a suitable migration approach must be decided before initiating the data import. A general approach that Temenos recommends is:

1. Analyse the legacy products and its parameters.
2. Create equivalent products in Temenos Asset Finance.
3. Determine the data that needs to be maintained in Temenos Asset Finance.
4. Prepare an extract of legacy contract data and balances. It must be in the prescribed format accepted by Temenos Asset Finance (Read working with section).
5. Migrate the following: Contract’s reference data such as customer data, currency, holiday records, limits, and collateral data, SSI (mandates for settlements such as direct debit standing order) and so on. Asset’s static data, depreciation schedule and balances. Contract’s static data such as contract term, amount, start date, payment schedule, settlement instruction and so on. Contract’s financial data such as outstanding principal, interest accruals (if any, delinquent balances).


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Migration feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Migration feature.

### 3.19  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Asset finance is a method of providing finance for hiring or purchasing tangible assets. The structure of the finance depends on the nature of the asset being purchased which ranges from cheaper and smaller items used in the day-to-day running business (such as a photocopier) to expensive and large-...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`, `EB.CONTEXT`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Asset finance is a method of providing finance for hiring or purchasing tangible assets. The structure of the finance depends on the nature of the asset being purchased which ranges from cheaper and smaller items used in the day-to-day running business (such as a photocopier) to expensive and large-scale assets with a long useful economic life (such as aircraft).

An asset finance arrangement is an agreement that outlines the terms and conditions under which one party agrees to hire asset(s) owned by another party. It allows to spread costs of an asset and avoid ownership cost. Asset finance also differs from a standard loan where an asset secures the finance agreement.

The following parties are involved in an asset finance agreement.

| Role | Description |
|---|---|
| Lessor | The party to a lease agreement who has legal or tax title to the asset, grants the lessee the right to use the asset for the lease term, and is entitled to the rentals. |
| Lessee | The user of the asset being leased (for example, customer). |
| Sub-Lessee | A lessee who re-leases to a third party and the lease agreement between the original lessee and lessor remains in effect. |
| Dealer | A person or entity who has a point of sales contact with the end customer and can conclude the agreement with the end customer on behalf of the lessor. |
| Supplier | A person or entity who delivers and is responsible for invoicing to the lessor the asset which is financed or other business services (this may or may not be identical to the vendor). |
| Vendor | A manufacturer, a distributor group, or a brand with whom the lessor enters a formal program relationship to support their sales. |

There may be several reasons for a business to hire an asset or equipment than to buy it outright. They are:

- Business needs the asset only for a short period.
- Asset Finance allows the business to keep in line with the latest technology.
- Financial institutions hold the risk and rewards incidental, such as maintenance of the asset.
- Asset finance is a solution for a business that needs equipment that is too costly to purchase outright.

In asset finance, the lessor gets the assured regular income by letting an asset. As ownership lies with the lessor, the tax benefit is applicable for the lessor through depreciation of the leased asset. This business is highly profitable for the lessor since the rate of return based on the lease rental is much higher than the interest payable on asset financing.

End-to-End Business

The end-to-end business process involved in asset finance is classified into the following:

- Sales and Marketing: It covers setting products and pricing model, channel availability, onboarding partner, managing opportunity pipelines, and revenue sharing.
- Transaction Process: It covers the activities from onboarding customer, credit analysis and approval, documentation, award to funding and servicing agreement till maturity.
- Support Process: It covers the various support functions involved in governing the above two processes, such as supplier management, treasury, risk management, data analytics and compliance, and reporting.

Asset Finance in Temenos Transact

Asset Finance (AS), a part of Transact Arrangement Architecture (AA), allows banks to define and launch products such as hire purchase, finance lease, contract hire/operating lease, fleet finance, and chattel mortgages for various asset classes, such as vehicles, equipment, plant and machinery, and land and buildings.

AS is built upon AA, therefore it possesses a product builder which caters for product condition re-usability, product families (that is, product inheritance), negotiation rules on all conditions, and product lifecycle management. Products are published in product catalogue.

Similar to other AA product lines, Asset Finance arrangements are also serviced through activities which can be backdated and reversed to any point of the arrangement. Transact automatically replays the activities considering the backdated or reversed activity. Additionally, activities can be forward dated.

This module covers the back-office servicing features that are related to contract management, lifecycles and workflows. Following are the main features of asset finance.

Product Management

- Allows rapid creation of new products and changes to existing products.
- Allows creation of product families and derivatives through inheritance and re-use of components.
- Supports product publishing, proofing, and product expiry.
- Supports rules-based eligibility criteria which allows the control of product availability to sub-sets of customers.

Pricing and Rate Cards

- Supports interest rates as fixed rate, variable rate (floating and periodic) based on index and margin.
- Allows to define and manage rate tiers based on finance amount.
- Supports periodic revision of interest rates based on a set frequency.
- Support penalty rates as contract rate and penalty spread.

Product Restrictions

- Allows to set up minimum and maximum finance amount for each product.
- Allows to set up minimum and maximum term for each product.
- Allows to set up minimum and maximum prepayment amount for each product.
- Allows to set up maximum prepayment for a rolling period or over life of agreement.
- Allows to set up allowed asset class and type for each product (say operating lease not allowed for trucks).
- Allows to set up product availability in channel(s), dealer(s) and so on.

Agreement

- Allows to create, activate and service the agreement.
- Allows to set up the term and conditions.
- Supports automatic and manual cancellation of agreement on a set period, if the arrangement is not activated on time.

Rental Calculations, Invoice or Billing and Settlement

- Supports various rental calculations such as annuity (constant), user (fixed), mixed payments (constant and fixed), Rule78, money factor, percentage (step-up or step-down), balloon payment.
- Supports flexible payment schedules with calculations based upon both standard and non-standard (for example, seasonal) frequencies.
- Supports collection of regular payments as either advance or arrears.
- Supports collection of ad-hoc payments.
- Supports invoice or billing and sends it to customer ’x’ days in advance before due date.
- Supports automatic recalculation of future payments and adjustment of future interest upon rate changes, prepayments, and so on.
- Allows to create receivables against invoice on the due date and initiate collection.
- Supports automatic collection of repayments from current or savings accounts maintained in the bank or from externally held accounts, through the payment solution.
- Supports repayments through online channels like branch, internet, local clearing, and so on.
- Supports automatic allocation of repayments towards principal, interest and charges based on rules ( by bill due date or by bill component).

Charges and Commission

- Allows to set up and collect ad-hoc event-based charges such as arrangement fee, delivery fee, admin fee, failed collection fee, payment return fee, and so on.
- Allows to set up and collect charges on a periodic basis along with regular payments such as maintenance fee.
- Supports to defer certain charges and collect along with first, next or last regular payment. For example, document fee on first instalment, purchase fee on last instalment, excess usage fee on next instalment.
- Supports recognition of charges and commission immediate into income or amortise over a term (maturity or specific period).
- Supports calculation of charges as flat, percentage and tiers (flat or band) based on amount, term.

Mid-life amendments

- Supports present, backed and future dated amendments.
- Supports automatic adjustments of balances and interest accruals for backdated amendments using reverse and replay technique.
- Supports almost every amendment to contract information, like, payment schedule amendments, settlement instructions, branch change request, term extension and so on.

Past due, Chaser

- Supports past due aging of bills based on either number of days past due or number of rentals past due.
- Allows to set up chase notice frequency and number of chasers for missed payments.
- Supports reporting of arrangements and balances with appropriate delinquent status based on days past due.
- Supports automatic suspension of unpaid and future income when arrangements go into non-accrual stage.
- Supports automatic upgrade to preforming status when past dues are fully settled and automatic resumption of income recognition.

Common features

- Supports fully compatible simulation processing.
- Supports ledger accounting.


##### Product Configuration

The following section describes the product configuration of AS.

Property Classes

Asset Finance product line provides high-level definitions of business components (property classes) required to deliver asset finance (leasing) functionality. The product line is system delivered and cannot be modified by the user.

The financial institution uses the business components to build individual and specific products based on the customer target segment requirements. The property classes of the Asset Finance product line are given below.

- Activity Charges
- Activity Mapping
- Activity Messaging
- Activity Presentation
- Charge
- Interest
- Officers
- Customer
- Payment Schedule
- Term Amount
- Payment Rules
- Overdue
- Settlement
- Reporting
- User Defined

Product Builder

Read AA Product Builder User Guide for more information on product construction and configuration process.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

Product conditions of a property class are evaluated to bring out the features of the property class. The values in the product condition are set to default in an arrangement during the arrangement creation. The negotiability and other restrictions are also defined in the product condition. These product conditions with the properties derived from the property classes are grouped together to build products.

Product conditions are dated and some of them have currency as part of their ID. If so, the user has to create different conditions for each currency in which the product is available. When a new condition is created or an existing condition is amended, the user has to proof and publish the product to which the condition is linked.

This property class is used to specify the account related information like description, title, category of the lease and so on. It is also used to create and maintain the lease account. Lease type classification is defined in this property class. It is also used to differentiate the asset using asset class and asset type.

This property class is used by all products. It defines the accounting rules for the leasing product and controls the link between the accounting events generated by the property actions and the accounting allocation rules to be applied to these events. Allocation rules such as lease principal and lease interest are used for accounting in leasing.

This property class allows the users to extend the core processing of arrangement activities by adding user-defined routines.

This property class defines the charges that must be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the lease contract. The applied charges can be set as due, capitalised or deferred.

This is an optional property class that allows the users to define versions used for various properties during arrangement activities. The versions can be defined at property class, property and activity levels.

This property class is used by all products. This property class is used to define all the parties involved in a contract. The customer is always defined at the contract level. Each contract can have one or more legal owners defined in owner(s), lessee or guarantor of the facility.

This property class is used to evaluate eligibility of a customer for a specific product based on a set of rules. Create the records in the EB.CONTEXT application in Temenos Transact. Based on these records, rules are defined using Rules Engine.

This property class is used to collect the mandatory documents required to manage the lease contract. The contract activation can be restricted based on conditions set by the lessor. The reports such as service reports, usage reports and so on can be maintained during the lease.

This property class is used to specify the lease rental rate, calculate everyday rental accrual and to collect the rentals from the lessee.

This property class allows the user to specify account officer or the relationship manager for the lessee(s).

This property class controls the ageing process of the bills raised in contract. The ageing period, statuses and accounting treatment of the outstanding balance can be defined. It is possible to define penalty interest to be applied on the overdue amounts and/or current balances. Bills can be aged based on the number of outstanding bills or days. It is also possible to define that all bills in a lease contract can be aged to the present status. Accounting entries can be raised for every status movement and chaser advices can be scheduled.

This property class controls the sequence and order in which the bills or outstanding balances that needs to be settled. An arrangement can contain several outstanding bills and each bill can comprise multiple amount (for example, principal, principal interest, penalty, tax, charges and so on). When a customer makes a payment, the entire due amount cannot be compromised. This property class is used to define the method by which a single payment is applied to multiple bills and multiple amount types.

This property class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is, made due or capitalised or pay). A payment schedule comprises of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as payment type and method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts.

The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types used by a product such as:

- Constant - Monthly
- Linear
- Percentage – Monthly
- Actual – Monthly and so on

Then, this payment type is attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified. The user can specify the rental repayment of arrangement based on the below-mentioned scenarios:

- To commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or
- To commence ‘n’ months before the maturity or
- To commence ‘n’ months after the change product, reset or rollover.

This property class is used for various product lines to control the settlement related functions of all the product lines. Settlement can be handled by linking any Temenos Transact account, the account and bank details of another bank by using direct debit and beneficiary of the customer.

This property class is used by financial products which involve the term and the lease amount of the contract. This property class controls the commitment made by the bank and the customer.

The user can add any additional user-defined property classes to the Asset Finance product line.

Contract Hire (Technology) Contract Hire (Trucks) Both Residual Amount and Guaranteed Residual Value cannot be used for Hire Purchase products Hire Purchase (Cars) Hire Purchase (Machinery) |

### 3.20  PaymentHoliday


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks or financial institutions can offer convenient repayment options for the customers. Asset Finance offers Payment Holiday feature that allows the banks/FIs to skip (payment deferral) or modify (increase or decrease) the scheduled payments based on the rules defined.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Holiday Restrict Item*, *Holiday Restrict Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks or financial institutions can offer convenient repayment options for the customers. Asset Finance offers Payment Holiday feature that allows the banks/FIs to skip (payment deferral) or modify (increase or decrease) the scheduled payments based on the rules defined.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes how to configure payment holidays.


##### Payment Holiday Property Class

The user can modify the scheduled payments either by skipping or modifying the payment amount. The Payment Holidays Transaction Property Class allows this type of flexible repayment plan. Product condition configuration is not required at the product level for Payment Holidays Property. The conditions need to be captured at arrangement level using the ASSET.FINANCE-UPDATE-PAYMENT.HOLIDAYS activity at the time of a payment holiday request. The subsequent changes to the payment holidays request can be made using the ASSET.FINANCE-CHANGE-PAYMENT.HOLIDAYS activity.

Read Payment Holiday for more information on the capability of Payment Holidays Transaction Class.


##### Restrictions on Payment Holidays

The banks or FIs can control the payment holiday feature with the following set of periodic attributes in the Payment Schedule condition.

| Periodic Attribute | Periodic Attribute Class | Functionality |
|---|---|---|
| HOLIDAYS.COUNT.YEARLY | HOLIDAYS.COUNT | Controls the number of payments skipped in a payment holidays request |
| HOLIDAYS.RESTRICT.LIFE | HOLIDAYS.RESTRICT | Restricts multiple payment holiday requests in the same holiday period. |

The Payment Schedule product condition can be configured with periodic attributes as below:

The Holiday Restrict Type and Holiday Restrict Item attributes in the Payment Schedule product condition can be configured to restrict specific components such as Payment Type, Bill Type, Property Class, Property in the payment holiday request.

Read Payment Holiday Restriction and Payment Holiday for more information on the Payment Holiday restrictions.


#### 📋 Tasks

Payment Holidays is one of the features offered by Asset Finance for the banks or FIs to skip (payment deferral) or modify (increase or decrease) the scheduled payments based on certain rules defined.


##### Workflow

In Payment Holiday, the user can perform the following activities:

This section covers the steps to request the Payment Holiday / Payment Deferral in the Asset Finance Arrangement.

1. Log in as BBOFFICER.
2. Asset Finance tab to search and view the asset finance arrangement.
3. Launch the Arrangement Overview from the enquiry result.
4. Click the Request Payment Holidays icon.
5. Select the payment date from which the payments need to be deferred.
6. Commit the activity.
7. Log in as BBMANAGER
8. Asset Finance tab to search and view the asset finance arrangement.
9. Launch the Arrangement Overview from the enquiry result.
10. Authorise the Payment Holiday Activity.


#### 📊 Outputs

Payment Holidays is one of the features offered by Asset Finance for the banks or FIs to skip (payment deferral) or modify (increase or decrease) the scheduled payments based on certain rules defined.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports:

#### 📖 Introduction

The Prepayment feature allows the lessee to prepay the outstanding balances. The prepayment quotation can be generated in the system for the required amount. The calculated prepayment amount includes unbilled principal and interest portion. Upon settling the prepayment quotation, the system recalculates the payment schedule for the current outstanding balance based on the recalculation setup.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In the Payoff product condition, the Payoff Settlement attribute needs to be defined as Partial to perform the early prepayment in the contract. The user can define the validity in number of days for the prepayment quotation in the Expiry Days attribute. The system sets the prepayment quotation to expire after a specified number of days, as determined by the Expiry Days attribute, starting from the prepayment quotation date. The user can settle the prepayment statement for the quoted prepayment amount before the prepayment statement’s expiry date.

Read Attributes in Payoff for more information.

The recalculation set up needs to be done for the payment rules activity (APPLYPAYMENT action) for the prepayment in the Payment Schedule product condition.


#### 📋 Tasks

### 3.22  Residual


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The residual amount or residual value represents the estimated value of the asset at the end of the finance agreement. The residual value can be classified as Guaranteed Residual and Unguaranteed Residual.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Arrangement ID*, *Asset Reference*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Guaranteed Percentage*, *Guaranteed Residual* ... +9 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The residual amount or residual value represents the estimated value of the asset at the end of the finance agreement. The residual value can be classified as Guaranteed Residual and Unguaranteed Residual.

Guaranteed Residual

The lessee can agree to guarantee the residual value of the asset as part of the asset finance agreement. In this case, the residual value is considered as Guaranteed Residual. If the market value of the asset goes below the guaranteed residual amount by the end of the agreement term, the lessee is obliged to pay the difference between the market value and the guaranteed residual amount.

Unguaranteed Residual

The asset finance agreement may state that the residual value is unguaranteed. In this case, the lessee is not responsible for guaranteeing a residual value at the end of the term. In operating lease, there is no financial obligation for the lessee at the end of the agreement term.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Residual Amount is an existing field in the Payment Schedule PC where the Residual Percentage , Guaranteed Residual , and Guaranteed Percentage attributes are used for configuring the residual functionality. In Asset Finance, the residual value can be defined as a flat amount or calculated based on the percentage of the commitment amount.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Residual Amount | Defines the expected residual value of the asset at the end of the contract term. |
| Residual Percentage | Defines the expected Residual Amount in percentage of the commitment amount at the end of contract term. |
| Guaranteed Residual | Defines the portion of the residual value that is guaranteed by the lessee. This value should be less than or equal to the Residual Amount . |
| Guaranteed Percentage | Defines the guaranteed residual value in percentage of the Residual Amount at the end of the contract’s term. |


#### 🔧 Working With

The residual amount and guaranteed residual can be defined as a flat amount and percentage of the asset cost. On the maturity date, the residual amount is handled based on the maturity options opted by the lessee. Refer Configuring Maturity Options section for more information.


##### Residual as Flat amount

The Residual Amount attribute in Payment Schedule PC is used to define the expected residual value of the asset at the end of the contract’s term. The residual amount can be defined as a flat amount using the residual amount attribute in Payment Schedule.

The residual amount is defined as USD 5,000 (Flat Amount)

The Term amount or Commitment amount is defined as USD 25,000 and the maturity option is chosen as Purchase the Asset.

The Residual amount is made due based on the maturity option opted by the Lessee.

If the residual amount defined is greater than the commitment amount, the system raises the validation error (Residual Amount should be lesser than the Term Amount).

The residual amount is defined as USD 30,000.

Upon validating the arrangement activity, system raises the error as shown below.


##### Residual as Percentage

The Residual Percentage attribute in Payment Schedule is used to define the expected residual amount in percentage of the term amount at the end of the contract’s term.

Upon defining the Residual Percentage as 20% for the asset finance arrangement with the commitment amount USD 25,000, the system calculates the residual amount as USD 5,000 and defaults in the Residual Amount attribute as shown below.


##### Guaranteed Residual as Fixed

The Guaranteed Residual attribute in Payment Schedule is used to define the residual value that is guaranteed by the lessee. It can be less than or equal to residual amount but not greater than the residual amount.

If the Guaranteed Residual amount defined is more than the Residual Amount, the system raises a validation error.

Upon validating the arrangement activity, the system raises an error as shown below.


##### Guaranteed Residual as Percentage

The Guaranteed Percentage attribute in the payment schedule is used to define the guaranteed residual value in percentage of the residual amount at the end of the contract’s term.

Upon defining the Guaranteed Percentage as 80% for the asset finance arrangement with Residual Amount USD 5,000, the system calculates the Guaranteed Residual amount as USD 4,500 and defaults in the Guaranteed Residual attribute as shown below.


##### Billing Residual Amount

The system makes the residual amount due during the maturity of the asset finance arrangement when the maturity option is set as Purchase the Asset.


##### Overdue

The Residual Amount bill undergoes overdue processing if the bill is not settled. Read Configuring Billing or Invoicing section for more information on Overdue processing in asset finance.


##### Settlement

The residual bill component in the final bill must be settled using the repayment activities like the other bills. Upon settling all the Residual Bill components, if there are no other due or overdue balance, the system moves the arrangement to the Pending Closure status.


#### 📋 Tasks

The residual amount or residual value represents the estimated value of the asset at the end of the finance agreement.

Residual Amount / Residual Percentage Guaranteed Residual / Guaranteed Percentage Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. Accept the overrides, if any. |

### 3.23  Restructure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Restructure feature allows the bank or financial institutions to reinstate the terminated contracts to current status with the term based on the agreement with the lessee or customer.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adv Payment Type*, *Adv Type Value*, *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Asset Reference*, *Context Name*, *Context Value*, *Currency* ... +10 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Restructure feature allows the bank or financial institutions to reinstate the terminated contracts to current status with the term based on the agreement with the lessee or customer.

Consider an asset finance arrangement is in three years term, the remaining term of the arrangement is two years. The lapsed term of the arrangement is one year, and the contract gets terminated after first year of the term.

- Post termination, if the term is defined as three years upon restructuring, the original term of the arrangement is derived, and the contract expires in another two years (considering the lapsed term as one year)
- Post termination, if the term is defined as two years upon restructuring, the arrangement expires in another one year (considering the lapsed term as one year)
- Post termination, if the term is defined as four years upon restructuring, the arrangement expires in another three years (considering the lapsed term as one year)

Upon restructuring, the new terms and conditions can be defined in the arrangement’s conditions such as Interest conditions, Payment Schedule conditions, Charge conditions, and so on, and the system recalculates the schedules based on the restructure activity’s arrangement conditions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The recalculation setup for the ASSET.FINANCE-RESTRUCTURE-ARRANGEMENT activity, which allows the system to recalculate the new payment plan with the current balances is defined in the Payment Schedule product condition. This activity can be triggered only on the terminated contract.

Read Termination for more information.


#### 📋 Tasks

The Restructure feature allows the bank or financial institutions to reinstate the terminated contracts to current status. Upon restructuring, new terms and conditions can be defined in the arrangement’s conditions such as Interest conditions, Payment Schedule conditions, Charge conditions and so on and the system recalculates the schedules based on the restructure activity’s arrangement conditions.

### 3.24  Schedule of Payments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Payments are regular fees or rent paid by the customer (lessee) to the lessor to be able to use the asset. The lessor who is the principal funding agent acquires the asset. The customer repays the capitalised cost of asset and interest premium, if any, in installments over the asset finance arrangem...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`, `AA.PROPERTY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Actual Amount*, *Bill Produced*, *Property Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Payments are regular fees or rent paid by the customer (lessee) to the lessor to be able to use the asset. The lessor who is the principal funding agent acquires the asset. The customer repays the capitalised cost of asset and interest premium, if any, in installments over the asset finance arrangement term. The receivable is the sum of the capitalised cost, interest premium and repayments towards the arrangement.

Payments are usually calculated as equal payments using the below formula

The lessee can have a custom schedule, which can include step-up, step-down, irregular payments and so on. The receivable (sum of the payments) remains the same throughout the term.

The asset finance arrangements are classified as either finance or operating lease where,

- The finance lease recognises the payments towards principal (asset's capitalised cost) and lease income (interest).
- The operating lease recognizes the payments towards the income and depreciation of an asset (that is, reduction of principal). It is made separately in the asset book usually on a straight-line basis over the asset’s usable life.

Although the recognition of payments and accounting is different for the operating and finance lease, the calculation of payments is based on the principal (cost of the asset), interest rate, term for both finance and operating leases.

The payments can be scheduled at regular intervals or ad-hoc payments. The accrued interest and charges are billed or invoiced to the lessee along with the principal in a regular payment frequency. The billed amount can be capitalised to the same asset finance arrangement or made due to be collected from the lessee’s account. The calculated amount can be waived, and the bill or offset bills can be deferred as required.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Payment Schedule property class is used to configure the payments. Most of the payment-related configurations for the asset finance contract are done in the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application and minimal information is entered at the contract creation level.

Select the payment type at the contract creation level and other details are defaulted from the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application.


##### Specifying Payment Method

The user can specify whether the due amount has to be paid by the lessee or capitalised to the lease principal, after specifying the payment type. The interest-only bills of the finance lease-type arrangement can also be capitalised to the principal. The capitalisation of interest is not applicable for operating lease contracts.

The charge can be scheduled either as due or capitalised into principal. The charges for both finance and operating lease arrangements can be capitalised.


##### Issuing Bill in Advance

Bills can be issued in advance by setting the Bill Produced attribute in the payment type record for all the payment types.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the scheduling of payments flow in an arrangement.


##### Scheduling Payments

The following payment types are supported in the asset finance product line as given in the table below:

| Payment Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Constant | Includes the principal and interest calculated on a reducing principal balance. This payment type is used for annuity payments and requires account and interest properties. |
| User Payments | The allowed user payment methods are: Constant - Payments that are calculated by an external source such as origination and fed in the system. The payment includes capital and interest. Interest is derived on a reducing capital balance and term. The Actual Amount attribute in the Payment Schedule property condition is used to enter this amount which is calculated externally. Actual - Payments that are calculated by an external system, which is used for operating lease and fed in the system. The payment includes only the interest or charge, which is fed by the external system. The Actual Amount attribute in the Payment Schedule property condition is used to enter this interest amount, which is calculated externally. The flat charge in the Charge product condition is used to enter the charge calculated in the external system. |
| Percentage | These are the constant payments calculated by the system with an option to specify the percentage of capital (asset cost) that must be recognised within each years. In this calculation type, the repayment is linearly distributed for the percentage defined over the period. The user can define step-up or step-down payments using the Percentage attribute in the Payment Schedule property class. |
| Actual | In this payment type, the payment amount is calculated by the system on an actual basis. It can be calculated based on the interest rate for interest-only payments and is defined as a flat amount or percentage of a specific balance for charge-only payments. |
| Linear | This payment type is used along with the interest-only and charge-only payments to define the fixed principal repayments. |
| Mixed Payments | In a single payment schedule, the user can define a specific amount for a period or set of periods and the remaining is calculated by the system using the annuity method. |


##### Handling Multiple Interest

Multiple interest rates can be defined for asset finance arrangements. Configure the Property Type for the interest as ‘Principal Receivable’ to support multiple interest definitions in the AA.PROPERTY application. Define the required properties in the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application. When the payment type record is used in the arrangement, the system calculates different interest amounts for different properties based on the interest rate in the Interest condition. The screenshot below shows the payment type record with multiple interest components.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Schedule of Payments feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Schedule of Payments defines the Dates, Total Due, Principal, Interest, and/or Charge portion of the payments for a specific Asset Finance arrangement. The bills are generated on or before the due date based on the configuration.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports:

Payment Schedule .

This enquiry displays the payments schedule for the asset finance arrangement.
